### 3.2.6 Compatibility Requirements

| Requirement | Source of Truth | Consequence if Violated |
|---|---|---|
| Python 3.12 interpreter | `pyproject.toml` `requires-python`, `python:3.12-alpine` base | Installation resolution failure; the CI 3.11/3.10 matrix legs are outside the supported set |
| Flask 3.1.x with Werkzeug ≥3.0.1 | `Flask>=3.1.1` plus explicit Werkzeug floor | Flask 3.1 requires modern Werkzeug/itsdangerous majors; the repository pins those floors explicitly rather than relying on resolution |
| WSGI callable named `application` | `wsgi.py` `__all__` | `gunicorn wsgi:app` (Dockerfile, README) cannot bind |
| `psutil` present wherever `wsgi.py` is imported | `wsgi.py` guarded import → `sys.exit(1)` | Production container built from root `requirements.txt` cannot start the WSGI module |
| `pytest-env` and `pytest-timeout` present wherever `pytest.ini` is honoured | `env =`, `timeout =` keys plus `--strict-config` | Test-configuration errors in strictly-provisioned environments |
| Flake8 and Black at a shared 88-column width | `.flake8` `max-line-length`, `[tool.black] line-length` | Formatter/linter conflict (avoided today by the matching values and the `E203/W503/W504` ignores) |
| Alpine package majors `curl=8.*`, `dumb-init=1.*`, `build-base=0.*`, `libffi-dev=3.*`, `openssl-dev=3.*` | `Dockerfile` L24–34 | Build failure when the upstream Alpine repository rotates those majors |

**Version-drift exposure.** Every dependency in every manifest uses an unbounded `>=` lower bound — a strategy stated explicitly at the end of `src/backend/requirements.txt`: "All version specifications use `>=` constraints to allow compatible minor and patch updates while maintaining stability and security". With no upper bounds and no lockfile, a fresh install resolves the newest release available at build time. For reference, <cite index="9-1">the latest Flask release line is 3.1.3</cite> and <cite index="8-3">Flask-CORS has since published a 6.0.5 wheel</cite> — meaning the `Flask-CORS>=4.0.0` floor permits a two-major-version jump that has never been validated against this codebase. `pyproject.toml` declares `[tool.pip-tools] generate-hashes = true`, but no compiled, hash-pinned artifact exists in the repository, so the intended mitigation is unimplemented.

### 3.2.7 Frameworks Deliberately Absent

For completeness, and consistent with `1.3 Scope`, the following framework categories were verified absent from every manifest and source file: ORM/data-mapper (SQLAlchemy and equivalents), migration tooling, schema/serialisation frameworks (marshmallow, pydantic), API documentation generators (OpenAPI/Swagger, Flask-RESTX), authentication frameworks (Flask-Login, Flask-JWT, Authlib, PyJWT), rate-limiting extensions, caching extensions (Flask-Caching), task/queue frameworks (Celery, RQ, APScheduler), async servers (uvicorn, hypercorn, ASGI adapters), and any frontend framework or bundler. `Jinja2` is present only as a Flask requirement — no template is rendered anywhere in `src/`.


## 3.3 Open Source Dependencies

Every third-party component in this system is an open-source Python distribution resolved from PyPI. Four declaration surfaces exist — three `requirements` files and the `pyproject.toml` extras — totalling **66 distinct packages** across 5 runtime, 41 backend-consolidated, and 44 development declarations.

### 3.3.1 Registry and Resolution Model

| Aspect | Observed Configuration |
|---|---|
| Registry | PyPI (default index). No `pip.conf`, `.netrc`, `PIP_INDEX_URL`, or private-index configuration exists anywhere in the repository |
| Installer | `pip`, always via `pip install -r <file>`; `README.md` documents `python3 -m venv` + activate + `pip install -r requirements.txt` |
| Version-pinning strategy | Exclusively unbounded lower bounds (`>=`). Stated policy at the end of `src/backend/requirements.txt`: "All version specifications use `>=` constraints to allow compatible minor and patch updates while maintaining stability and security" |
| Lockfile | **None.** No `requirements.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `Pipfile.lock`, `uv.lock`, or hash-pinned compiled requirements. `pyproject.toml` declares `[tool.pip-tools] generate-hashes = true`, `upgrade = false`, `quiet = 1`, but no compiled artifact was ever committed |
| Build isolation | `[build-system] requires = ["setuptools>=68.0", "wheel>=0.42.0", "setuptools-scm>=8.0"]`, `build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"` |
| Caching | `actions/setup-python@v4/@v5` with `cache: 'pip'` keyed on `requirements.txt` + `requirements-dev.txt`; `actions/cache@v3` on `~/.cache/pip`; Compose named volumes `pip_cache_dev` / `pip_cache_prod` |
| Offline capability | None. `1.3 Scope` records air-gapped installation as unsupported: every documented path resolves from PyPI |

### 3.3.2 Runtime Dependencies — `requirements.txt` (5 packages)

This is the manifest consumed by the container `dependencies` stage and by both CD smoke-test jobs, so it defines the production closure.

| Package | Constraint | Recorded Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Flask | `>=3.1.1` | WSGI framework replacing Express.js v5.1.0 |
| python-dotenv | `>=1.0.1` | Twelve-factor `.env` configuration replacing `process.env` |
| Flask-CORS | `>=4.0.0` | Cross-origin handling that Express provided natively |
| gunicorn | `>=21.2.0` | Production WSGI server with multi-worker management |
| wheel | `>=0.42.0` | Faster installation and distribution of packages |

`psutil` is **not** in this list, although `wsgi.py` imports it unconditionally — see `3.2.3`.

### 3.3.3 Backend Consolidated Manifest — `src/backend/requirements.txt` (41 packages)

This manifest is a superset covering runtime, testing, quality, security, and container concerns in one file. It is what `.github/workflows/ci.yml` *appears* to target (`working-directory: src/backend`) although the steps actually install the root-level files.

| Group | Packages and Constraints |
|---|---|
| Production runtime | `Flask>=3.1.1`, `python-dotenv>=1.0.1`, `Flask-CORS>=4.0.0`, `gunicorn>=21.2.0` |
| Testing and QA | `pytest>=8.4.0`, `pytest-flask>=1.3.0`, `coverage>=7.6.0`, `pytest-cov>=5.0.0`, `pytest-benchmark>=4.0.0`, `pytest-xdist>=3.5.0`, `psutil>=5.9.0`, `Faker>=22.0.0` |
| Code quality and security | `black>=24.0.0`, `flake8>=7.0.0`, `bandit>=1.7.5`, `safety>=3.0.0`, `mypy>=1.8.0`, `flake8-security>=1.7.1` |
| Development utilities | `python-multipart>=0.0.6`, `watchdog>=3.0.0`, `wheel>=0.42.0`, `pytest-html>=4.1.0`, `pytest-mock>=3.12.0`, `requests>=2.31.0`, `jsonschema>=4.20.0` |
| Container and deployment | `packaging>=23.0` (annotated "Ensure compatibility with `python:3.12-alpine` base image"), `build>=1.0.0` |
| Explicit transitive floors | see `3.3.5` |

This manifest is additive tooling only — it contains no runtime packages — and is installed by the CI `test` job and by the container `development` stage.

### 3.3.5 Explicitly Declared Transitive Floors

`src/backend/requirements.txt` contains a section titled "PINNED VERSIONS FOR SECURITY AND REPRODUCIBILITY" that re-declares packages Flask, pytest, and the tooling would install anyway. Declaring them raises their floors deliberately for security reasons.

| Package | Floor | Annotation in the manifest |
|---|---|---|
| Werkzeug | `>=3.0.1` | "Flask dependency with security fixes" |
| Jinja2 | `>=3.1.2` | "Flask templating engine with security patches" |
| MarkupSafe | `>=2.1.3` | "Safe string handling for Jinja2" |
| itsdangerous | `>=2.1.2` | "Cryptographic signing for Flask sessions" |
| click | `>=8.1.7` | "Command line interface library used by Flask" |
| pluggy | `>=1.3.0` | pytest plugin system |
| iniconfig | `>=2.0.0` | pytest configuration parsing |
| tomli | `>=2.0.1` | TOML parsing for `pyproject.toml` support |
| certifi | `>=2023.11.17` | "Certificate bundle for HTTPS requests" |
| urllib3 | `>=2.1.0` | "HTTP library with security updates" |
| idna | `>=3.6` | Internationalised domain names |
| pathspec | `>=0.12.0` | Path specification parsing for black |
| platformdirs | `>=4.1.0` | Platform-specific directory discovery |
| typing-extensions | `>=4.8.0` | Typing extensions for mypy |

Two Flask requirements are **not** floor-pinned here — `blinker` and `importlib-metadata` — so the security-floor list is incomplete relative to <cite index="9-1">Flask's declared required dependencies (blinker, click, importlib-metadata, itsdangerous, jinja2, markupsafe, werkzeug)</cite>.

### 3.3.6 Manifest Divergence and Declared-But-Unused Packages

Because the same tools are declared in three or four places with different floors, "the version of X" is not single-valued:

| Package | Root / Backend | `requirements-dev.txt` | `pyproject.toml` |
|---|---|---|---|
| bandit | `>=1.7.5` | `>=1.8.3` | `>=1.7.5` |
| safety | `>=3.0.0` | `>=3.0.0` | `>=3.0.1` |
| pip-audit | — | `>=2.6.0` | `>=2.6.1` |
| isort | — | `>=5.13.0` | `>=5.13.2` |
| psutil | `>=5.9.0` | `>=5.9.0` | `>=5.9.6` |
| pytest-html | `>=4.1.0` | `>=4.1.1` | `>=4.1.1` |
| Faker | `Faker>=22.0.0` | `faker>=20.0.0` | — |
| sphinx | — | `>=7.2.0` | `>=7.2.6` |

Twenty-two packages appear in `src/backend/requirements.txt` but not in `requirements-dev.txt`, and twenty-five appear in `requirements-dev.txt` but not in `src/backend/requirements.txt` — so neither file is a superset of the other and the installed set depends on which file a given job or build stage happens to use.

A substantial share of declared packages are never imported by any file under `src/`: `Faker`/`faker`, `jsonschema`, `python-multipart`, `responses`, `vcrpy`, `factory-boy`, `freezegun`, `orjson`, `pytest-mock`, `pytest-tmp-path`, `docker`, `gitpython`, `sphinx`, `sphinx-rtd-theme`, `pylint`, `pydocstyle`, `ipython`, `ipdb`, `ptpython`, `flask-debugtoolbar`, `memory-profiler`, `line-profiler`, `types-flask`, `types-requests`, and `pre-commit` (for which no `.pre-commit-config.yaml` exists). The actually-imported third-party set is small: `flask`, `flask_cors`, `dotenv`, `psutil`, `pytest`, and `requests`.

### 3.3.7 Supply-Chain Security Posture

| Control | Implementation | Gate Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Static application security testing | `bandit` (`pyproject.toml` `[tool.bandit]` excludes `tests`, `venv`, `build`, `dist`, `htmlcov`; skips `B101`, `B601`, `B602`) | `ci.yml` generates JSON+SARIF non-blocking (`|| true`), then `bandit -r src/ --severity-level medium` blocks; `quality-gate` fails on any HIGH finding |
| Dependency vulnerability scanning | `safety` and `pip-audit` | Report generation non-blocking; the follow-up `safety check --short-report` and bare `pip-audit` invocations gate. `cd.yml` fails the security gate when Safety reports any vulnerability |
| Container image scanning | `aquasecurity/trivy-action@master` against the published digest, severities `CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW`, `exit-code: '0'` | SARIF parsed by `jq`; gate fails on `CRITICAL > 0`, warns on `HIGH > 5` or Bandit issues > 3 |
| Repository posture | `ossf/scorecard-action@v2` with `publish_results: true` | Advisory; SARIF uploaded |
| Provenance and SBOM | `docker/build-push-action@v5` with `provenance: true` and `sbom: true` | Attestations attached to the published image only — no SBOM is committed to the repository |
| Findings aggregation | `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2` (Bandit, pip-audit, Scorecard in CI; Trivy under category `container-security` in CD) | GitHub code scanning |

**Residual supply-chain risks**, all evidenced above: no lockfile or hash pinning, unbounded upper bounds on 66 packages, a floating `@master` reference for the Trivy action, a `skip_tests` workflow-dispatch input in `cd.yml` that bypasses the entire security-scan job for "emergency deployments", and non-blocking report-generation steps that mask scanner crashes.


## 3.4 Third-Party Services

The application itself consumes **no third-party service at runtime**: `src/backend/app.py` and `src/backend/wsgi.py` make no outbound network calls, hold no API client, and read no service credential. Every third-party service in this stack is a *platform* or *toolchain* service exercised by the two GitHub Actions workflows and the container assets — consistent with the integration landscape described in `1.2 System Overview`.

### 3.4.1 Service Integration Inventory

| Service | Category | Integration Point | Version / Identifier | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub Actions | CI/CD platform | `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/cd.yml` | `ubuntu-latest` runners; `[tool.ci] github_actions = true` | Test, scan, quality-gate, build, deploy |
| GitHub Container Registry | Container registry | `cd.yml` `env: REGISTRY: ghcr.io`, `IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}` | `docker/login-action@v3`, `docker/build-push-action@v5` | Multi-architecture image publication (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) with provenance and SBOM attestations |
| Azure Web Apps | Cloud application hosting | `azure/webapps-deploy@v2` in `deploy_staging` and `deploy_production` | Apps `flask-tutorial-staging` and `flask-tutorial-production` | Container hosting for the two deployment environments |
| Codecov | Coverage reporting | `codecov/codecov-action@v3` in the CI `test` job | `file: src/backend/coverage.xml`, `flags: unittests`, `name: codecov-python-${{ matrix.python-version }}`, `fail_ci_if_error: false` | Per-Python-version coverage publication |
| GitHub code scanning | Security findings aggregation | `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2` | CI uploads Bandit + pip-audit + Scorecard SARIF; CD uploads Trivy SARIF under category `container-security` | Centralised vulnerability visibility |
| OSSF Scorecard | Supply-chain posture assessment | `ossf/scorecard-action@v2` with `publish_results: true` | `scorecard-results.sarif` | Repository security-practice scoring |
| Aqua Security Trivy | Container vulnerability scanning | `aquasecurity/trivy-action@master` (unpinned) | Scans `ghcr.io/<repo>@<digest>`, severities `CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW` | Image CVE detection feeding the CD security gate |
| PyPI | Package registry | `requirements*.txt`, `pyproject.toml` | Default index | Dependency resolution and vulnerability auditing inputs |
| Docker Hub | Base-image source | `Dockerfile` `FROM python:3.12-alpine`; Compose `image: alpine:3.19`, `cache_from: python:3.12-alpine` | Official images | Runtime and utility base layers |
| Read the Docs | Documentation hosting (declared only) | `pyproject.toml` `[project.urls] Documentation = "https://flask-migration-tutorial.readthedocs.io/"` | — | Referenced URL; no Sphinx source tree exists in the repository |

### 3.4.2 Cloud Services

Azure Web Apps is the only cloud runtime target implemented anywhere in the repository. Its configuration is entirely literal — there are no inputs, variables, or IaC definitions.

| Aspect | Staging | Production |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub environment | `staging` | `production` |
| Environment URL | `https://flask-tutorial-staging.azurewebsites.net` | `https://flask-tutorial.azurewebsites.net` |
| Azure app name | `flask-tutorial-staging` | `flask-tutorial-production` |
| Deployed artifact | `${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}@${{ needs.build_and_publish.outputs.image_digest }}` — immutable digest, not a tag | same digest |
| Injected environment | `FLASK_ENV=production`, `FLASK_DEBUG=false`, `PORT=8000`, `LOG_LEVEL=info`, `TUTORIAL_ENVIRONMENT=staging`, `GUNICORN_WORKERS=2`, `GUNICORN_TIMEOUT=30` | `FLASK_ENV=production`, `FLASK_DEBUG=false`, `PORT=8000`, `LOG_LEVEL=info`, `TUTORIAL_ENVIRONMENT=production` |
| Initialisation wait | `sleep 45` | `sleep 75` |
| Gate to enter | CI success plus a passing security scan | Release publication or manual dispatch, plus `deploy_staging.outputs.deployment_status == 'success'` and `security_scan.outputs.scan_result != 'failed'` |

Note the port convention here: Azure deployments inject `PORT=8000`, which matches the application defaults in `app.py`/`wsgi.py` but not the container's `EXPOSE 3000` and `--bind=0.0.0.0:3000`. `1.3 Scope` records the 3000/5000/8000 divergence as a known inconsistency.

No other cloud provider is integrated. `src/backend/.env.example` contains commented deployment examples for Heroku, Render, and Railway, and `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` treats "production deployment to a chosen platform" as deferred work — so those are options, not integrations. There is no AWS, GCP, S3/Blob storage, CDN, DNS, load-balancer, or serverless configuration anywhere in the repository, and `infrastructure/` contains only `docker/`.

### 3.4.3 Authentication and Credential Model

There are two distinct authentication concerns, and only one of them exists.

**Application-level authentication: none.** No identity provider, OAuth/OIDC client, JWT library, session login, or API-key store is present. `src/backend/README.md` documents `/hello` as "Authentication: None required", and `1.3 Scope` lists authentication and authorization as explicitly excluded. `src/backend/.env.example` includes a commented `JWT_SECRET_KEY` / `JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRES` block labelled "Authentication Configuration Example (not used in tutorial)". The only cryptographic material the application touches is Flask's `SECRET_KEY`, read at `app.py` from `os.getenv('SECRET_KEY', 'dev-key-change-in-production')` — a plain environment variable with a development fallback and no secrets-manager integration.

**Pipeline-level authentication: GitHub-native secrets only.**

| Credential | Consumer | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` | `docker/login-action@v3` for `ghcr.io`; `TRIVY_PASSWORD` for registry-authenticated scanning; SARIF upload | Ephemeral, workflow-scoped |
| `secrets.AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE_STAGING` | `azure/webapps-deploy@v2` (staging) | Not present in the repository; must be configured in GitHub |
| `secrets.AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE_PRODUCTION` | `azure/webapps-deploy@v2` (production) | Not present in the repository; must be configured in GitHub |
| GitHub `environment:` protection on `staging` / `production` | `deploy_staging`, `deploy_production` | The only approval/gating mechanism; no external change-management integration |

`2.4 Implementation Considerations` records that these registry and Azure credentials are outstanding human tasks, so the CD pipeline is structurally complete but not operable as committed.

### 3.4.4 Monitoring, Observability and Health Services

Runtime observability is entirely self-contained; no APM or telemetry vendor is integrated.

| Mechanism | Implementation | Destination |
|---|---|---|
| Application logging | `logging.basicConfig` at INFO with `%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s`; `wsgi.py` attaches handlers for both stdout and stderr | Container stdout/stderr only — no log shipper, aggregator, or sink |
| Request correlation and timing | `after_request` emits `X-Request-ID` (`req_<epoch-ms>`) and `X-Response-Time` | Response headers and INFO logs |
| Process memory | `psutil` RSS/VMS sampling in `wsgi.py` with a 75 MB warning threshold | Application logs and test assertions |
| Liveness probing | `HEALTHCHECK` on `/hello` — 30 s/10 s/3 retries with a 15 s start period in production, 15 s/5 s/2 retries in development; Compose repeats the same probes | Docker/orchestrator health status |
| Deployment health validation | `cd.yml` staging loop of 12 attempts with 20 s back-off and `--max-time 15`; production loop of 18 attempts with 25 s back-off and `--max-time 20`, matching the `/hello` body | Job outputs |
| Post-deployment monitoring | Production `monitoring` step polls `/hello` and sets `rollback_required=true` when the failure rate exceeds **20 %** | `deploy_production.outputs.rollback_required` |
| Smoke-test performance thresholds | Staging warns when a single `/hello` request exceeds **3.0 s**; production warns when the average of repeated requests exceeds **1.5 s** (warnings only, non-blocking) | Job logs |
| Coverage telemetry | Codecov plus 30-day CI artifacts (`htmlcov/`, `coverage.xml`, `pytest_report.html`, `junit.xml`) and 90-day security-report artifacts | Codecov, GitHub artifacts |

No alerting or on-call routing exists: health results gate deployment and container restart policy only.

### 3.4.5 Service Categories Verified Absent

An exhaustive grep across all source files and manifests for thirty service/SDK identifiers returned matches **only** inside documentation prose, commented `.env.example` examples, and ignore-file patterns. The following are therefore confirmed absent as integrations: identity providers (Auth0, Okta, Cognito, LDAP/OIDC), payment or messaging providers, email/SMS services, external business APIs, message brokers and event streams (Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS), secrets managers (Vault, Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager), APM and tracing vendors (Sentry, Datadog, New Relic, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus), feature-flag services, CDN/WAF services, and AI/LLM services (OpenAI, LangChain). `.gitignore` and `.dockerignore` reference names such as `newrelic` and `prometheus` purely as artifact-exclusion patterns inherited from generic templates.


## 3.5 Databases &amp; Storage

**This system has no database and no persistence tier.** That is a design property rather than an omission: `1.3 Scope` lists data persistence, ORM/migrations, and caching layers as explicitly excluded, and `2.4 Implementation Considerations` notes that `/health` performs no dependency checks "because the service has no dependencies". This sub-section documents what the repository does contain in place of a data layer.

### 3.5.1 Verification of the Absent Persistence Tier

| Technology Class | Search Result |
|---|---|
| Relational drivers / ORM | No `sqlalchemy`, `flask-sqlalchemy`, `psycopg`, `asyncpg`, `mysqlclient`, or `sqlite3` usage or declaration |
| Document stores | No `pymongo`, `motor`, or MongoDB reference outside documentation prose |
| Key-value / cache backends | No `redis`, `pymemcache`, or `Flask-Caching` declaration |
| Migration tooling | No `alembic`, `Flask-Migrate`, or `migrations/` directory (`.flake8` merely lists `migrations` as a generic exclusion pattern) |
| Object storage SDKs | No `boto3`, `azure-storage-blob`, or `google-cloud-storage` |
| Schema artifacts | No `.sql`, `.ddl`, seed, or fixture data files anywhere in the repository |

The only database vocabulary in the repository is instructional: `src/backend/.env.example` carries a commented block headed "Database Configuration Example (not used in tutorial)" containing `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `DATABASE_SSL_MODE`, and `SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI`, plus a separate "Redis Configuration Example (not used in tutorial)" block with `REDIS_URL`, `REDIS_PASSWORD`, `REDIS_DB`, and `CELERY_BROKER_URL`. None of these names is read by any code path.

### 3.5.2 Data Handling and Persistence Strategy

The persistence strategy is **stateless request-scoped computation**. All data is synthesised per request and discarded when the response is written.

| Data Element | Origin | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|
| `message` (`Hello world`) | Compile-time literal in `hello_route_handler` (`app.py` L358 onward) | Response only |
| `timestamp` | `datetime` ISO-8601 formatting at handler time | Response only |
| `status` | Literal | Response only |
| `uptime`, `version` (`1.0.0`), `environment`, `debug` | `health_check_handler`; `uptime` is the raw `time.time()` epoch value | Response only |
| `X-Request-ID` (`req_<epoch-ms>`) and `start_time` | Attached to the Flask request context by `before_request` (`app.py` L291) | Request context only |
| Session data | **Never written.** Session cookie policy is configured per profile (`SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`, `HTTPONLY`, `SAMESITE=Lax`, `PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME` 3600 s production / 86400 s development) but no code writes to `session` |

Statelessness is asserted, not assumed: `2.4 Implementation Considerations` records that `TestFlaskStatelessOperation` verifies repeated requests return an identical payload and that no mutable module-level state is shared. The practical consequence for the stack is that horizontal scaling requires no shared store, no sticky sessions, and no cache-coherency protocol. Inbound data volume is bounded by `MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH = 16 * 1024 * 1024` (16 MB), which is the only storage-adjacent resource control in the application.

### 3.5.3 Caching Solutions

There is no cache *server*. Caching exists at two other levels.

**HTTP response caching directives (application-level):**

| Directive | Value | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `/health` cache policy | `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` | `health_check_handler` — deliberately uncacheable so probes always reflect current state |
| CORS preflight cache | `max_age: 86400` (24 h) | `configure_cors_middleware` — reduces `OPTIONS` traffic but delays propagation of allow-list changes by up to a day |
| Static-file cache age | `SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT: 31536000` (1 year) in the WSGI production profile | `wsgi.py` L171 — configured but inert, since no static assets exist |

**Build and dependency caching (toolchain-level):**

| Cache | Mechanism | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| pip download cache | `actions/setup-python` `cache: 'pip'` keyed on both requirements files; `actions/cache@v3` on `~/.cache/pip` keyed by `runner.os` + Python version + `hashFiles(...)` | CI jobs |
| Docker layer cache | `docker/build-push-action@v5` with `cache-from: type=gha` and `cache-to: type=gha,mode=max` | CD image build |
| Compose build cache | `cache_from: [python:3.12-alpine, flask-tutorial:dev-cache | flask-tutorial:prod-cache]` | Local builds |
| Virtual-environment and pip volumes | Named volumes `venv_cache_dev`, `venv_cache_prod`, `pip_cache_dev`, `pip_cache_prod` | Local Compose runs |

### 3.5.4 Container Storage Topology

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph DevService["Compose service flask-tutorial-dev"]
        DevApp["/usr/src/app<br/>bind mount, consistency delegated<br/>source: ../../src/backend"]
        DevVenv["/usr/src/app/.venv<br/>named volume venv_cache_dev"]
        DevPip["/home/python/.cache/pip<br/>named volume pip_cache_dev"]
    end

    subgraph ProdService["Compose service flask-tutorial-prod"]
        ProdRoot["root filesystem<br/>read_only: true<br/>*.py at mode 444"]
        ProdTmp["tmpfs /tmp and /var/tmp<br/>rw, size=10M, mode=1777"]
        ProdVenv["/usr/src/app/.venv<br/>venv_cache_prod, read_only"]
        ProdPip["/home/python/.cache/pip<br/>pip_cache_prod, read_only"]
    end

    subgraph NamedVolumes["Docker named volumes, driver local"]
        VolDevVenv["flask-tutorial-venv-dev-cache"]
        VolProdVenv["flask-tutorial-venv-prod-cache"]
        VolDevPip["flask-tutorial-pip-dev-cache"]
        VolProdPip["flask-tutorial-pip-prod-cache"]
        VolShared["flask-tutorial-shared<br/>declared but mounted by no service"]
    end

    HostSrc["Host: src/backend/*.py"] -->|"hot reload"| DevApp
    DevVenv --> VolDevVenv
    DevPip --> VolDevPip
    ProdVenv --> VolProdVenv
    ProdPip --> VolProdPip
    VolShared -.->|"unused"| ProdService
```

Key properties of this topology:

- **Production is immutable by construction.** `read_only: true` at the container level, `chmod -R 444 *.py` in the Dockerfile `production` stage, read-only volume mounts, `cap_drop: ALL` with only `SETGID`/`SETUID` restored, `no-new-privileges:true`, and execution as `user: "1000:1000"`. Writable space is limited to two 10 MB tmpfs mounts. `2.4 Implementation Considerations` notes the `apparmor:unconfined` setting as an acknowledged educational compromise.
- **Development trades isolation for iteration speed.** The delegated bind mount of `../../src/backend` onto `/usr/src/app` enables `--reload` hot reloading, and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=0` in that stage allows `.pyc` writes.
- **No application data volume is in use.** `flask_shared_data` (`flask-tutorial-shared`, labelled `tutorial.purpose=educational-persistence`) is declared in the `volumes:` block but is not referenced by either application service — the repository contains no path that persists application state.
- **Resource envelope.** The production service is capped at `memory: 128M` / `cpus: '0.5'` with reservations of `75M` / `0.25`, aligning the container budget with the 75 MB process budget enforced by `psutil` and the test suite.

### 3.5.5 Generated Artifact Storage

The only files the system writes are verification and reporting outputs, all reproducible and all git-ignored.

| Artifact | Produced By | Retained Where |
|---|---|---|
| `htmlcov/`, `coverage.xml`, `coverage.json` | `pytest-cov` per both `pytest.ini` files | Working tree; uploaded as `coverage-reports-python-<version>` for 30 days |
| `junit.xml`, `pytest_report.html` | `--junit-xml`, `--html --self-contained-html` | Working tree; uploaded as `test-results-python-<version>` for 30 days |
| `benchmark_results.json` | `pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest-benchmark] json_output` | Working tree |
| `tests.log` (root) and `logs/pytest.log` (backend) | pytest `log_file` at DEBUG | Working tree |
| `bandit-report.{json,sarif}`, `safety-report.json`, `pip-audit-report.{json,sarif}`, `scorecard-results.sarif` | CI `security` job | Artifact `security-reports`, 90 days, plus GitHub code scanning |
| `trivy-results.sarif`, `bandit-results.json`, `safety-results.json` | CD `security_scan` job | Artifact `python-security-scan-results`, 30 days |
| Container images | `docker/build-push-action@v5` | `ghcr.io` with digest-addressed immutability, provenance and SBOM attestations |
| `.pytest_cache/` | pytest `cache_dir` | Working tree, ignored |

`pyproject.toml` `[tool.ci] artifact_retention_days = 30` documents the intended default, which the workflows honour except for the 90-day security-report retention. The declared coverage configuration file `.coveragerc` — referenced by root `pytest.ini` via `--cov-config=.coveragerc` — does not exist, so coverage settings resolve from `[tool.coverage.*]` in `pyproject.toml` or from defaults instead.


## 3.6 Development &amp; Deployment

Development and delivery tooling is the largest part of this stack by volume: 1,422 lines of GitHub Actions YAML, 874 lines of Docker assets, and 1,008 lines of test/lint/packaging configuration support 1,280 lines of application and test code. Every tool below is declared in the repository; where a tool is configured but never invoked, that is stated explicitly.

### 3.6.1 Local Development Toolchain

| Tool | Version Requirement | Role | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPython | ≥ 3.12.0 (recommended "Latest 3.12.x") | Interpreter | `README.md` System Requirements table |
| pip | ≥ v23.0.0 | Package installation | `README.md`; `pip install --upgrade pip>=24.0` in the Dockerfile `dependencies` stage |
| `venv` | stdlib | Environment isolation | `python3 -m venv .venv` then `source .venv/bin/activate` (macOS/Linux) or `.venv\Scripts\activate` (Windows) — `README.md`, `src/backend/README.md` |
| pyenv | referenced | Optional interpreter version management | `README.md` Installation Links |
| Flask CLI | via `click>=8.1.7` | Development server | `python -m flask run` with `FLASK_APP=app.py`; `flask run --host=localhost --port=3000` documented in `src/backend/README.md` |
| Gunicorn | `>=21.2.0` | Local production-parity run | `gunicorn wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:3000 --workers 4` (`src/backend/README.md`) |
| watchdog | `>=3.0.0` | Filesystem-event hot reload | Declared in all dev manifests; installed in the container `development` stage |
| debugpy | `>=1.8.0` | Remote/IDE debugging | Installed in the Dockerfile `development` stage; exposed on port 5678 and mapped by Compose |
| curl | `8.*` (Alpine) | Health probing | `Dockerfile` `apk add`; used by every `HEALTHCHECK` |
| Docker / Docker Compose | referenced (`docs.docker.com/get-docker`) | Optional containerised workflow | `README.md`; `infrastructure/docker/` |
| Environment template | — | Configuration bootstrap | `src/backend/.env.example` documents the seven supported variables with validation guidance (`PORT` 1024–65535; `FLASK_ENV` ∈ {development, production, testing}; `FLASK_DEBUG` truthy set) |

**Developer-onboarding inconsistency.** `README.md` and `src/backend/README.md` describe the Python workflow, but `CONTRIBUTING.md` is still titled "Contributing to Node.js Hello World Tutorial", carries Node v22.16.0 LTS and Express v5.1.0 badges, and references `npm` 28 times and Jest 12 times against only a single mention of Python; `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` similarly favours npm/Jest terminology. A contributor following the governance documents would provision the wrong toolchain entirely.

### 3.6.2 Code Quality and Static Analysis Tooling

| Tool | Constraint | Configuration | Invoked by CI? |
|---|---|---|---|
| flake8 | `>=7.0.0` | `.flake8`: `max-line-length = 88`; `select = E,W,F,C,S,N,I`; `max-complexity = 10`, `max-annotations-complexity = 4`, `max-expression-complexity = 7`, `max-cognitive-complexity = 12`; ignores `E203,E501,W503,W504,E402,D100–D105`; per-file test ignores | **Yes** — `flake8 . --config=.flake8 --statistics --count` |
| flake8-security | `>=1.7.1` | Supplies the `S` codes selected in `.flake8` | Yes, transitively through flake8 |
| black | `>=24.0.0` | `pyproject.toml` `[tool.black]`: `line-length = 88`, `target-version = ["py312","py313"]`, `preview = false`, `fast = false`, excludes `infrastructure`, caches, and build output | **No workflow step invokes it** |
| isort | `>=5.13.0`/`>=5.13.2` | `profile = "black"`, `line_length = 88`, `known_first_party = ["src","app","backend"]`, `known_third_party = ["flask","pytest","coverage","psutil","gunicorn"]`, `force_sort_within_sections = true` | **No** |
| mypy | `>=1.8.0` | `python_version = "3.12"`; `check_untyped_defs`, `no_implicit_optional`, `warn_unreachable`, `strict_equality`, `extra_checks` enabled; `disallow_untyped_defs = false`; `ignore_missing_imports = true` with per-module overrides for `flask.*`, `pytest.*`, `coverage.*`, `psutil.*`, `gunicorn.*` and relaxed rules for `tests.*` | **No** |
| pylint / pydocstyle | `>=3.0.0` / `>=6.3.0` | No configuration and no invocation | No |
| bandit | `>=1.7.5` / `>=1.8.3` | `[tool.bandit]` excludes `tests`, `venv`, `.venv`, `build`, `dist`, `.pytest_cache`, `htmlcov`; skips `B101`, `B601`, `B602` | **Yes** — blocking at `--severity-level medium`, plus a HIGH-severity gate in `quality-gate` |
| safety | `>=3.0.0`/`>=3.0.1` | — | **Yes** — `safety check --short-report` blocking |
| pip-audit | `>=2.6.0`/`>=2.6.1` | — | **Yes** — bare `pip-audit` blocking |
| pre-commit | `>=3.6.0` | **No `.pre-commit-config.yaml` exists** | No |

The consequence is a two-tier quality regime: lint and security analysis are enforced gates, while formatting, import ordering, and type checking are documented conventions only. `2.4 Implementation Considerations` records adding Black/isort/mypy invocations as outstanding work.

### 3.6.3 Test Execution Configuration

Two `pytest.ini` files exist and both shadow the `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` block in `pyproject.toml`.

| Setting | Root `pytest.ini` | `src/backend/pytest.ini` |
|---|---|---|
| `testpaths` | `src/backend/tests` | `tests` |
| Coverage target | `--cov=src/backend` | `--cov=src` |
| Strictness | `--strict-markers --strict-config` | same |
| Coverage gate | `--cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` plus `--cov-context=test`, `--no-cov-on-fail`, `--cov-config=.coveragerc` (**file absent**) | `--cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` |
| Reports | term-missing, `html:htmlcov`, `xml:coverage.xml`, `json:coverage.json` | same plus `--junit-xml=junit.xml`, `--html=pytest_report.html`, `--self-contained-html` |
| Timeout | `timeout = 300`, `timeout_method = thread` | same |
| `minversion` | `8.0` | `7.0` |
| `required_plugins` | pytest-flask ≥1.3.0, pytest-cov ≥5.0.0, pytest-benchmark ≥4.0.0, pytest-xdist ≥3.5.0, pytest-html ≥4.1.1 | pytest-flask ≥1.3.0, **pytest-cov ≥6.1.0**, pytest-html ≥4.1.0 |
| Markers | 17 (unit, integration, performance, security, smoke, regression, slow, network, docker, benchmark, memory, load, health, e2e, flaky, xfail, parametrize, fixture) | 10 (unit, integration, performance, security, smoke, slow, flask, wsgi, health, error) |
| Warning policy | selective ignores; `error::pytest.PytestConfigWarning` | `error` first (all warnings fatal) then ignores for `UserWarning`, `DeprecationWarning:flask.*`, `PendingDeprecationWarning` |
| Test environment | `FLASK_ENV=testing`, `TESTING=1`, `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED=False`, `SECRET_KEY=testing-secret-key-not-for-production`, `LOG_LEVEL=ERROR` | same minus `SECRET_KEY` |
| Logging | `log_cli` INFO; `log_file = tests.log` at DEBUG; `junit_family = xunit2`, `junit_logging = all`, `showlocals = true` | `log_cli` INFO; `log_file = logs/pytest.log` at DEBUG |

Because marker sets differ and `--strict-markers` is active in both, a test marked with a root-only marker (for example `@pytest.mark.load`) fails when run under the backend configuration. There is also no `conftest.py` anywhere — fixtures are defined inline in each test module.

### 3.6.4 Build System and Packaging

| Element | Configuration |
|---|---|
| Standard | PEP 518 build system + PEP 621 metadata in `pyproject.toml` |
| Backend | `setuptools.build_meta` with `setuptools>=68.0`, `wheel>=0.42.0`, `setuptools-scm>=8.0` |
| Package layout | `[tool.setuptools] package-dir = {"" = "src"}`, `include-package-data = true`, `zip-safe = false`; `packages.find` scans `src` excluding `tests*`; `package-data` includes `*.txt, *.md, *.yml, *.yaml, *.json, *.cfg, *.ini` |
| Versioning | Static `version = "1.0.0"` in `[project]`, while `[tool.setuptools_scm]` declares `write_to = "src/_version.py"`, `version_scheme = "python-simplified-semver"`, `local_scheme = "no-local-version"` — the two mechanisms coexist and `src/_version.py` is not committed |
| Build driver | `build>=1.0.0`; documented usage `python -m build` |
| Distribution | No wheel/sdist is published by any workflow; the delivered artifact is the container image |

Note that the packaging layout (`package-dir = {"" = "src"}`) implies importable modules under `src/`, whereas the application actually lives at `src/backend/` and imports itself flatly (`from app import create_app`). Packaging and runtime import strategies are therefore not aligned — the same root cause as the divergent test import paths.

### 3.6.5 Containerization

`infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile` defines a four-stage build on `python:3.12-alpine`:

| Stage | Base | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| `base` | `python:3.12-alpine` | `apk` security upgrade plus `curl=8.*`, `dumb-init=1.*`, `build-base=0.*`, `libffi-dev=3.*`, `openssl-dev=3.*`; `WORKDIR /usr/src/app`; non-root `python` user/group at UID/GID 1000; `ENV PYTHONPATH=/usr/src/app PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHON_VERSION=3.12 PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 FLASK_ENV=production FLASK_APP=app.py PORT=3000 HOST=0.0.0.0`; `USER python` |
| `dependencies` | `base` | Copies both requirements files; creates `/usr/src/app/.venv`; upgrades pip and installs `wheel`; installs `requirements.txt`; verifies `flask.__version__` and `gunicorn.__version__` via `python -c` |
| `application` | `dependencies` | Copies only `app.py` and `wsgi.py`; `EXPOSE 3000`; `HEALTHCHECK` 30 s/10 s/10 s/3 on `/hello`; `CMD dumb-init sh -c "… python -m flask run --host=0.0.0.0 --port=3000"` |
| `development` | `dependencies` | `FLASK_ENV=development`, `FLASK_DEBUG=1`, `LOG_LEVEL=debug`; installs `requirements-dev.txt` and verifies pytest/pytest-flask/coverage; copies full `src/backend/` plus `tests/`; installs `debugpy>=1.8.0` and `watchdog>=3.0.0`; `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=0`; `EXPOSE 5678`; `HEALTHCHECK` 15 s/5 s/5 s/2; `CMD … debugpy --listen 0.0.0.0:5678 --wait-for-client -m flask run … --debug --reload` |
| `production` | `application` | `FLASK_DEBUG=0`, `LOG_LEVEL=info`, `WORKERS=4`, `WORKER_CONNECTIONS=1000`, `MAX_REQUESTS=1000`, `MAX_REQUESTS_JITTER=100`, `TIMEOUT=30`, `KEEPALIVE=2`; cleans `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, `/root/.cache`; `HEALTHCHECK` 30 s/10 s/15 s/3; `chmod -R 444 *.py`; `GUNICORN_CMD_ARGS` and a Gunicorn `CMD` |

Design choices worth noting: `dumb-init` is PID 1 so SIGTERM reaches Gunicorn and the handlers in `wsgi.py`; the build uses a virtual environment *inside* the image rather than a distroless copy-out, which is why every `CMD` activates `.venv` through `sh -c`; and `build-base`/`libffi-dev`/`openssl-dev` remain in the final image because `production` derives from `application` rather than a clean stage.

`infrastructure/docker/docker-compose.yml` (Compose file format `3.8`) adds the local topology: `flask-tutorial-dev` (ports 3000 and 5678, delegated source bind mount, hot reload), `flask-tutorial-prod` (host 3001 → container 3000, read-only root filesystem, tmpfs scratch, 128 M/0.5 CPU limits, `replicas: 1`, rolling update with `failure_action: rollback`, restart policy 3 attempts in a 120 s window), and `flask-network-setup` (an `alpine:3.19` utility service that documents the bridge network). All services run as `user: "1000:1000"` on the `flask-tutorial-network` bridge and carry `tutorial.framework=flask.3.1.1` / `tutorial.runtime=python.3.12` labels. `infrastructure/docker/.dockerignore` (762 lines) trims the build context — excluding `.git`, virtual environments, package caches, all `.env` files, keys and certificates, and IDE configuration.

### 3.6.6 Continuous Integration Pipeline

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — "CI Pipeline", three jobs on `ubuntu-latest`.

| Aspect | Configuration |
|---|---|
| Triggers | `push` to `main`/`develop` filtered on `src/backend/**`, `tests/**`, `requirements.txt`, `requirements-dev.txt`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`; `pull_request` to `main` (`opened`/`synchronize`/`reopened`); weekly `schedule` cron `0 2 * * 1`; `workflow_dispatch` |
| Concurrency | `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true` |
| Global env | `FLASK_ENV=testing`, `CI=true`, `COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=100`, `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, `PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=false`, `PIP_UPGRADE_STRATEGY=eager`, `FORCE_COLOR=1` |
| `test` (15 min) | Matrix `['3.12','3.11','3.10']`; `actions/checkout@v4` (`fetch-depth: 0`), `actions/setup-python@v4` with pip caching, `actions/cache@v3`; installs both root requirements files; runs flake8 then pytest with the 100 % gate; publishes to `codecov/codecov-action@v3`; uploads coverage and test artifacts via `actions/upload-artifact@v3` (30 days) |
| `security` (10 min) | Python 3.12; installs `bandit[toml] safety pip-audit`; Bandit JSON+SARIF non-blocking then blocking `--severity-level medium`; Safety and pip-audit likewise report-then-gate; `ossf/scorecard-action@v2`; SARIF via `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2`; 90-day security artifacts |
| `quality-gate` (10 min, `needs: [test, security]`) | Downloads `coverage-reports-python-3.12` and `security-reports`; installs `coverage[toml] lxml`; heredoc-generates `scripts/validate_coverage.py` which parses `../coverage/coverage.xml` and fails when line- or branch-rate < `COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=100`; inline Python fails on any HIGH Bandit finding or any Safety vulnerability |

Two structural defects: every step sets `working-directory: src/backend` while installing root-level manifests, and the coverage-validation step writes into a `scripts/` directory that does not exist in the repository and reads a path neither `pytest.ini` produces.

### 3.6.7 Continuous Deployment Pipeline

`.github/workflows/cd.yml` — "CD Pipeline", five jobs on `ubuntu-latest`.

| Aspect | Configuration |
|---|---|
| Triggers | `workflow_run` on workflows `["CI Pipeline"]`, types `[completed]`, branches `[main]`; `release` `[published]`; `workflow_dispatch` with `environment` (choice `staging`/`production`), `image_tag` (default `latest`), and `skip_tests` (boolean, "Skip security scanning for emergency deployments") |
| Concurrency | `cd-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false` |
| Global env | `REGISTRY=ghcr.io`, `IMAGE_NAME=${{ github.repository }}`, `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1`, `COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1`, `FLASK_ENV=production`, `FLASK_DEBUG=false`, `TUTORIAL_VERSION="2.0.0"` |
| `build_and_publish` (20 min) | Runs when dispatched, released, or `workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`. `docker/setup-buildx-action@v3`, `docker/login-action@v3`, `docker/metadata-action@v5`, `docker/build-push-action@v5` building `target: production` for `linux/amd64,linux/arm64` with `cache-from/to: type=gha`, `provenance: true`, `sbom: true`; outputs `image_digest` |
| Image tagging | Branch/PR refs with `-python` suffix; `type=sha` with `{{branch}}-python-` prefix and a timestamp suffix; semver `{{version}}`/`{{major}}.{{minor}}`/`{{major}}` each `-python`-suffixed; `latest-python` on the default branch; `tutorial-python-{{date 'YYYYMMDD'}}` |
| Image labels | Full `org.opencontainers.image.*` set (title, description, vendor, version, created, revision, url, source, documentation) plus `tutorial.framework=flask`, `tutorial.runtime=python`, `tutorial.version=3.1.1`, `tutorial.educational=true` |
| `security_scan` (15 min) | Skipped when `inputs.skip_tests == 'true'`. Bandit and Safety report generation, then `aquasecurity/trivy-action@master` on the digest with `exit-code: '0'`; `jq` maps SARIF levels to severity counts; fails on `CRITICAL > 0` or any Safety vulnerability, warns on `HIGH > 5` or Bandit issues > 3 |
| `deploy_staging` (12 min) | GitHub `environment: staging`; `azure/webapps-deploy@v2` to `flask-tutorial-staging` using the digest; 45 s initialisation wait; 12-attempt `/hello` health loop with 20 s back-off; five smoke tests covering body, status code, content type, response time (< 3.0 s warning), `/health`, and the 404 path |
| `deploy_production` (18 min) | Requires `deploy_staging.outputs.deployment_status == 'success'` and a non-failed scan; `environment: production`; `azure/webapps-deploy@v2` to `flask-tutorial-production`; 75 s wait; 18-attempt health loop with 25 s back-off; repeated-request average latency warning above 1.5 s; monitoring loop sets `rollback_required=true` above a 20 % failure rate |
| `deployment_notification` (5 min, `if: always()`) | Builds a markdown status summary of all jobs and uploads it as an artifact |

The pipeline's version-extraction step greps `^Flask==` in `requirements.txt`; because the manifest declares `Flask>=3.1.1`, the hard-coded `3.1.1` fallback always supplies the reported version.

### 3.6.8 End-to-End Delivery Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Trigger["Developer push / PR to main<br/>weekly cron 0 2 * * 1<br/>manual dispatch"]

    subgraph CIStage["CI Pipeline — ci.yml"]
        TestJob["test<br/>matrix 3.12 / 3.11 / 3.10<br/>flake8 + pytest --cov-fail-under=100"]
        SecJob["security<br/>bandit + safety + pip-audit + Scorecard"]
        GateJob["quality-gate<br/>coverage 100% line and branch<br/>zero HIGH bandit findings"]
    end

    subgraph CDStage["CD Pipeline — cd.yml"]
        BuildJob["build_and_publish<br/>buildx multi-arch, target=production<br/>provenance + SBOM"]
        ScanJob["security_scan<br/>Trivy on image digest<br/>gate: CRITICAL = 0"]
        StageJob["deploy_staging<br/>12-attempt health loop<br/>5 smoke tests"]
        ProdJob["deploy_production<br/>18-attempt health loop<br/>rollback flag above 20% failures"]
        NotifyJob["deployment_notification<br/>always()"]
    end

    Registry["ghcr.io<br/>digest-addressed image<br/>linux/amd64 + linux/arm64"]
    AzStaging["Azure Web App<br/>flask-tutorial-staging"]
    AzProd["Azure Web App<br/>flask-tutorial-production"]
    CodeScan["GitHub code scanning<br/>SARIF: bandit, pip-audit, Scorecard, Trivy"]
    Codecov["Codecov<br/>per-Python-version coverage"]

    Trigger --> TestJob
    Trigger --> SecJob
    TestJob --> GateJob
    SecJob --> GateJob
    TestJob --> Codecov
    SecJob --> CodeScan
    GateJob -->|"workflow_run conclusion success on main"| BuildJob
    BuildJob --> Registry
    Registry --> ScanJob
    ScanJob --> CodeScan
    ScanJob --> StageJob
    StageJob --> AzStaging
    StageJob -->|"release published or manual dispatch"| ProdJob
    ProdJob --> AzProd
    StageJob --> NotifyJob
    ProdJob --> NotifyJob
```

### 3.6.9 Integration Requirements and Toolchain Gaps

Operating this stack end to end requires the following, none of which is satisfiable from the repository alone:

1. **Registry and cloud credentials.** `secrets.AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE_STAGING` and `..._PRODUCTION` must be configured, and the two Azure Web Apps must exist with the hard-coded names. `2.4 Implementation Considerations` records both as outstanding human tasks.
2. **A consistent WSGI callable reference.** Either rename the export or fix `Dockerfile` L220 (`gunicorn wsgi:app`) and the equivalent `README.md` command; the Compose production command is already correct.
3. **`psutil` in the runtime manifest**, or `wsgi.py` must stop importing it — otherwise the production image cannot start the WSGI module.
4. **`pytest-timeout` and `pytest-env` in whichever manifest a given environment installs**, because both `pytest.ini` files depend on their ini options under `--strict-config`.
5. **Port convention convergence.** `.env.example` and all container assets use 3000, the application modules default to 8000, Azure injects `PORT=8000`, and `README.md` examples use 5000.
6. **The referenced-but-absent artifacts**: `.coveragerc`, `src/backend/scripts/`, `LICENSE`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and a Sphinx documentation source tree for the declared Read the Docs URL.
7. **CI matrix alignment** with `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, and `working-directory` correction so the manifests being installed are the ones the steps intend.
8. **Formatting and typing enforcement** if `black`, `isort`, and `mypy` are meant to be gates rather than conventions.

Two further tools are declared with no supporting configuration and therefore contribute nothing today: `pip-tools>=7.3.0` (with `generate-hashes = true` but no compiled output) and `pre-commit>=3.6.0` (with no hook configuration). Finally, there is no infrastructure-as-code layer at all — `infrastructure/` contains only `docker/`, so Azure resource provisioning, networking, and TLS remain entirely manual.

# 4. Process Flowchart

## 4.1 System Workflows

This section documents the executable process flows of the repository as they are actually implemented. The runtime surface is deliberately small — two `GET` endpoints served by a two-module Flask application (`src/backend/app.py`, 750 lines; `src/backend/wsgi.py`, 530 lines) — so the workflow set is dominated by *lifecycle* and *delivery* processes rather than by multi-step business transactions.

Three scoping facts govern every diagram below and are stated once here rather than repeated:

| Scoping Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| There is no persistence tier, message broker, or outbound network call, so no workflow contains a database write, queue publish, or third-party API step | `requirements.txt` declares only `Flask`, `python-dotenv`, `Flask-CORS`, `gunicorn`, `wheel`; `src/backend/.env.example` marks its `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `CELERY_BROKER_URL`, and `API_BASE_URL` blocks "not used in tutorial" |
| There is no authentication, authorization, or user identity, so no workflow contains a login, token, or permission step | No auth code exists in `src/backend/`; `src/backend/app.py` accepts `Authorization` as a CORS-allowed header name only |
| Asynchronous behaviour is limited to POSIX signal delivery and Python's uncaught-exception hook; there is no scheduler, worker pool, or event bus inside the application | `src/backend/wsgi.py` L192–255 (`setup_signal_handlers`), L432–474 (`handle_uncaught_exceptions`) |

Section 2.2.1.2 already presents the request pipeline as a single linear flowchart. The workflows below extend that view with actor swim lanes, sequence-level interaction detail, batch/pipeline sequences, and the failure and recovery branches that the linear view omits.

### 4.1.1 Core Business Processes

#### 4.1.1.1 Workflow Inventory and Actors

Eight distinct end-to-end processes are implemented in the repository. Every one is traceable to a file, and every one has an identifiable terminal state.

| Workflow | Trigger | Primary Actor | Terminal States |
|---|---|---|---|
| W-1 First-run onboarding to first response | Human clones the repository | Learner / contributor | Verified `Hello world` response, or a filed bug report |
| W-2 Process bootstrap and WSGI initialization | Module import by a WSGI server, or direct execution | Gunicorn / Python interpreter | `application` callable exported, or `sys.exit(1)` / chained `RuntimeError` |
| W-3 Greeting request-response cycle | `GET /hello` | HTTP client | HTTP 200 JSON, or a 4xx/5xx JSON envelope |
| W-4 Health probe cycle | `GET /health` | Container runtime, CD gate, test readiness loop | HTTP 200 `healthy`, or HTTP 503 `unhealthy` |
| W-5 Error dispatch and response shaping | Unmatched route, disallowed method, or raised exception | Flask error dispatcher | Uniform JSON error envelope with correct status code |
| W-6 Graceful shutdown | `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`, `SIGUSR1`, `SIGUSR2`, or uncaught exception | Container orchestrator / operator / interpreter | Cleanup logged, final memory sample taken, process terminated by its parent |
| W-7 Continuous integration batch | Push, pull request, weekly cron, or manual dispatch | GitHub Actions | `quality-gate` passed, or a failing job |
| W-8 Continuous deployment batch | Successful CI on `main`, published release, or manual dispatch | GitHub Actions + Azure Web Apps | Production healthy, `rollback_required=true`, or `PARTIAL`/`FAILED` report |

The actors that appear as swim lanes across the diagrams in this section are: the **learner/contributor** (human touchpoints), the **HTTP client** (`curl`, browser, `requests`, Flask test client), the **process runtime** (`dumb-init` at PID 1 plus the Gunicorn master and its sync workers), the **Flask application** (factory, hooks, routes, error handlers), and the **delivery platform** (GitHub Actions, `ghcr.io`, Azure Web Apps).

#### 4.1.1.2 High-Level System Workflow

The following swim-lane flowchart is the master view: it connects the human onboarding path, the process bootstrap sequence, the request-serving pipeline, and the operational/delivery lane, showing where each lane hands control to the next.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Client(["HTTP client<br/>curl / browser / requests"])

    subgraph LaneDev["Lane 1 — Contributor and learner touchpoints"]
        D1(["git clone repository"])
        D2["Create .venv and<br/>pip install -r requirements.txt"]
        D3["Copy .env.example to .env<br/>seven documented variables"]
        D4{"Run locally or<br/>open a pull request?"}
```

Two boundaries are worth naming explicitly because they determine ownership of failures. First, `src/backend/wsgi.py` reads and validates `HOST` and `PORT` but never binds a socket — binding belongs to the WSGI server, so a port conflict surfaces from Gunicorn, not from application code. Second, `perform_graceful_shutdown()` never calls `sys.exit()`; final termination is performed by `dumb-init`/Gunicorn, which is why the container `CMD` entries in `infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile` place `dumb-init` at PID 1.

#### 4.1.1.3 W-1 — End-to-End Onboarding Journey with Error Recovery

This is the only workflow with a human in the loop at every step. Timing expectations are documented rather than enforced: `src/backend/.env.example` states that environment processing completes in "< 0.2 seconds" with "< 2KB" overhead, and the `performance_baseline` fixture in `src/backend/tests/test_wsgi.py` (L307–312) records a `cold_start_ms` threshold of 100 ms.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Begin(["Learner begins onboarding"])
    Begin --> Chk1{"Python 3.12 or newer<br/>and pip available?"}
    Chk1 -->|"No"| Fix1["Install from python.org or pyenv<br/>per README prerequisites table"]
    Fix1 --> Chk1
    Chk1 -->|"Yes"| Step1["Create and activate .venv"]
    Step1 --> Step2["pip install -r requirements.txt:<br/>Flask, python-dotenv, Flask-CORS,<br/>gunicorn, wheel"]
    Step2 --> Chk2{"Third-party imports<br/>resolve at module load?"}
    Chk2 -->|"No"| Err1["Guarded import block prints the exact<br/>pip install command; app.py re-raises<br/>ImportError, wsgi.py calls sys.exit(1)"]
    Err1 --> Step2
    Chk2 -->|"Yes"| Step3["Copy .env.example to .env:<br/>PORT, HOST, FLASK_ENV, FLASK_DEBUG,<br/>LOG_LEVEL, WORKERS, SECRET_KEY"]
    Step3 --> Mode{"Which run mode?"}
    Mode -->|"Flask dev server"| RunA["python app.py<br/>HOST localhost, PORT 8000, debug True,<br/>use_reloader False"]
    Mode -->|"WSGI module direct"| RunB["python wsgi.py<br/>dev server started only when<br/>FLASK_ENV equals development"]
    Mode -->|"Production WSGI"| RunC["gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:8000<br/>wsgi:application"]
    Mode -->|"Containers"| RunD["docker compose up:<br/>dev on 3000, prod on 3001 mapped to 3000"]
    RunA --> Bind{"Configuration valid and<br/>port bindable?"}
    RunB --> Bind
    RunC --> Bind
    RunD --> Bind
    Bind -->|"No"| Err2["ValueError for PORT outside 1 to 65535;<br/>startup exception logged with three<br/>troubleshooting hints: port in use,<br/>env vars, factory failure"]
    Err2 --> Step3
    Bind -->|"Yes"| Ready(["Startup banner logs PID, platform,<br/>and both endpoint URLs"])
    Ready --> Verify["curl http://HOST:PORT/hello"]
    Verify --> Result{"HTTP 200 with<br/>message Hello world?"}
    Result -->|"Yes"| Done(["Onboarding complete;<br/>X-Response-Time visible on the response"])
    Result -->|"No"| Triage["File issue with bug_report.md:<br/>auto-labelled bug and needs-triage;<br/>template includes Flask-specific<br/>troubleshooting sections"]
    Triage --> Done
```

The four run modes are not equivalent, and the differences are load-bearing for support questions: `python app.py` defaults `HOST` to `localhost` while `create_wsgi_application()` defaults it to `0.0.0.0`; `src/backend/.env.example` sets `PORT=3000` while both modules default to `8000`; and all container ports use 3000. A learner following the container path and the code path simultaneously will observe two different ports.

#### 4.1.1.4 W-3 and W-4 — Request-Response Interaction Sequence

The sequence below is the per-request contract, expressed at the level of the individual hooks and handlers registered by `create_app()`. Note the response-finalization order: `configure_security_settings()` registers its `after_request` hook *before* `register_middleware_hooks()` registers the timing hook, and Flask executes `after_request` callbacks in reverse registration order, so timing and correlation headers are written first and the security headers are applied last — guaranteeing that even error envelopes carry all six headers.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as HTTP client
    participant G as Gunicorn sync worker
    participant W as wsgi.py application callable
    participant BR as before_request hook
    participant RT as Route handler
    participant EH as Error handlers
    participant AR as after_request pipeline
    participant LG as stdout and stderr logs

    C->>G: GET /hello or GET /health
    G->>W: WSGI environ and start_response
    W->>BR: request dispatched into the Flask app
    BR->>LG: INFO Incoming request with method and path
    BR->>BR: set start_time and correlation id req_ plus epoch ms
    alt POST or PUT carrying a non-JSON body
        BR->>LG: WARNING non-JSON request detected
        Note over BR: request is NOT rejected, control returns None
    end
    BR->>RT: URL rule and method matched
    alt Handler completes normally
        RT->>LG: INFO 200 OK with response payload summary
        RT-->>AR: 200 JSON body plus X-API-Version on /hello
    else Route handler raises internally
        RT-->>AR: handler-local 500 JSON envelope
    else No rule, wrong method, or exception escapes
        RT->>EH: Flask error dispatch
        EH->>LG: WARNING for 404 and 405, ERROR for 500
        EH-->>AR: uniform JSON envelope with status and timestamp
    end
    AR->>AR: write X-Response-Time and X-Request-ID
    AR->>AR: Flask-CORS decorates allowed origins
    AR->>AR: remove Server and set six security headers
    AR->>LG: INFO Request completed with status and duration
    AR-->>G: finalized response object
    G-->>C: HTTP response, warm target under 50 ms
```

For `GET /health` the same pipeline applies with two differences: the handler adds `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` so that probes are never served from an intermediary cache, and its `except` branch returns HTTP 503 with `status: unhealthy` instead of delegating to the 500 handler. The handler performs no dependency checks — there are no dependencies to check.

#### 4.1.1.5 Consolidated Decision Points

Every conditional branch in the runtime path is enumerated below with its evidence location and its consequence. This is the authoritative decision-point register for the workflows in 4.1.1.

| Decision Point | Location | Branches and Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Third-party imports available? | `app.py` L40–49; `wsgi.py` L35–43, L47–53 | Available → continue. Missing → print remediation, then `raise ImportError` (`app.py`) or `sys.exit(1)` (`wsgi.py`) |
| Which environment profile? | `app.py` L169, L182, L194 | `production` / `development` / `testing` each apply a distinct config block; **no `else` branch** — an unrecognised name silently receives base configuration only |
| `FLASK_DEBUG` truthy? | `app.py` L156 | Only the exact lower-cased string `true` enables debug, although `.env.example` documents `true`, `1`, `yes`, `on` |
| `PORT` numeric and in range? | `wsgi.py` L299–331 | In 1–65535 → return int; below 1024 → warn and continue; otherwise → chained `ValueError` aborting startup |
| Module executed or imported? | `wsgi.py` L479 vs. L518 | `__main__` → install excepthook, signals, app, optional dev server. Imported → signals and app only, **excepthook not installed** |
| `FLASK_ENV == development` at `__main__`? | `wsgi.py` L497 | Yes → start the Flask development server. No → log Gunicorn guidance and exit the block |
| Non-JSON body on `POST`/`PUT`? | `app.py` L318–320 | Warning logged; request proceeds unchanged (no rejection) |
| URL rule matched? | Flask routing | `/hello` → greeting handler; `/health` → health handler; otherwise → 404 handler |
| Method allowed for the matched rule? | Flask routing + `app.py` L518 | Allowed → handler; disallowed → 405 with `allowed_methods` and an `Allow` header when `error.valid_methods` is present |
| `app.config['DEBUG']` set during error handling? | `app.py` L580–581, L619–620 | True → full traceback logged server-side. False → traceback suppressed; client payload is generic either way |
| `start_time` / `id` present on the request? | `app.py` L336, L347 | Present → emit `X-Response-Time` / `X-Request-ID`. Absent → header omitted, no failure |
| RSS above 75 MB? | `wsgi.py` L362–366 | Above → WARNING "exceeds 75MB target". At or below → INFO confirmation. Advisory only at runtime |
| Signal platform-supported? | `wsgi.py` L243–246 | `SIGUSR1`/`SIGUSR2` registered only when `hasattr(signal, ...)`; `OSError` during registration downgrades to a warning |
| `KeyboardInterrupt`? | `wsgi.py` L452–454 | Yes → delegate to `sys.__excepthook__` and return. No → log, sample memory, graceful shutdown |
| `flask_app` instantiated at shutdown? | `wsgi.py` L273 | Yes → log application cleanup. No → skip that stage; the remaining shutdown steps still run |

#### 4.1.1.6 Error-Handling Paths in the Core Processes

Each core process has exactly one designed failure exit. The table records the observable outcome; the mechanisms (retries, fallbacks, notification, recovery) are detailed in 4.3.2.

| Workflow | Failure Trigger | Observable Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| W-2 Bootstrap | Missing dependency | Remediation text on stdout, then process exit code 1 |
| W-2 Bootstrap | Invalid `PORT` | `ValueError` chained into startup failure; no app object created |
| W-2 Bootstrap | Any factory-stage exception | `RuntimeError` chained from the original cause, after logging four troubleshooting hints |
| W-3 Greeting | Exception inside the handler | Handler-local HTTP 500 JSON `{status: error, message, timestamp}` |
| W-4 Health | Exception inside the handler | HTTP 503 JSON `{status: unhealthy, error, timestamp}` |
| W-5 Error dispatch | Unmatched path | HTTP 404 JSON echoing only the caller's own `path` and `method` |
| W-5 Error dispatch | Disallowed method | HTTP 405 JSON plus `Allow` header |
| W-5 Error dispatch | Escaped exception | HTTP 500 or `Exception`-handler JSON with a fixed generic message and `request_id` |
| W-6 Shutdown | Exception during cleanup | Logged as `"Error during graceful shutdown"`; never re-raised |
| W-6 Shutdown | Uncaught exception in-process | Logged, memory sampled, dev-only traceback, then graceful shutdown as `UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION` |

### 4.1.2 Integration Workflows

#### 4.1.2.1 Integration Surface and Data Flow Between Systems

The application is a pure sink for inbound HTTP and a pure source of logs, headers, and process metrics. Every integration that crosses a system boundary is either inbound HTTP or part of the toolchain/delivery chain.
