## 6.6 Testing Strategy

### 6.6.1 Testing Approach Assessment and Scope

#### 6.6.1.1 Applicability Determination

By functional scope alone, this system would not warrant a comprehensive testing strategy. The application is a single stateless Flask process exposing two anonymous `GET` routes — `/hello` (`src/backend/app.py` L367) and `/health` (L426) — with no datastore, no authentication, no message broker, no downstream API, no user interface, and no business domain. The repository's own retained pre-migration specification states this explicitly: `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications_b3815ee7-12a2-46a4-a950-4b8e72ef8030.md` L3543-L3545 opens its section 6.6 with the heading *"Detailed Testing Strategy is not applicable for this system"* and argues that a tutorial with one endpoint returning a static greeting does not require complex integration testing, end-to-end frameworks, or enterprise-grade automation.

**That determination does not describe the repository as delivered.** The migration to Python replaced the Jest-era plan with a genuinely multi-layer pytest apparatus that is *larger than the application it tests* and is enforced by blocking pipeline gates. A full testing strategy is therefore documented here — not because the endpoint is complex, but because the test apparatus, its thresholds, its automation, and its gates all exist in the repository and are load-bearing for the delivery pipeline. Where a topic from the standard testing taxonomy has no counterpart in this system (database integration, UI automation, cross-browser coverage), that is stated plainly in the relevant sub-section rather than filled with generic material.

| Assessment Dimension | Functional Reality | Delivered Test Apparatus |
|---|---|---|
| Endpoints under test | 2 (`/hello`, `/health`) | 36 test functions across 13 test classes |
| Integration points | None (no datastore, queue, or external API) | Real Gunicorn subprocess integration, 100-request load tests |
| Test code volume | 1,280 lines of runtime code (`app.py` 750 + `wsgi.py` 530) | 2,117 lines of test code (`test_app.py` 712 + `test_wsgi.py` 1,405) |
| Enforcement | Educational tutorial, no external users | 100 % line **and** branch coverage gate, five security scanners, blocking release gates |

#### 6.6.1.2 Test Asset Inventory

Every testing asset in the repository is listed below. There are no other test files, fixture files, helper packages, or test tooling directories.

| Asset | Location | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Application test suite | `src/backend/tests/test_app.py` (712 L) | Factory, route, error-handler, security-header, performance, statelessness, middleware and configuration tests |
| WSGI/deployment test suite | `src/backend/tests/test_wsgi.py` (1,405 L) | Gunicorn lifecycle, signal handling, port binding, WSGI integration, benchmark, memory, load and full-lifecycle E2E tests |
| Primary pytest configuration | `pytest.ini` (245 L, repo root) | Discovery, coverage gate, 18 markers, test env vars, JUnit settings |
| Backend pytest configuration | `src/backend/pytest.ini` (297 L) | Alternate discovery/reporting profile with 10 markers, used when pytest runs inside `src/backend` |
| Declarative pytest/coverage config | `pyproject.toml` L156-L284 | Third pytest profile plus the authoritative `[tool.coverage.*]` settings |
| Lint policy for tests | `.flake8` per-file-ignores | Relaxes `E501,F401,F403,S101,S311,D100-D103` for `tests/*.py`, `test_*.py`, `**/test_*.py` |
| Test-capable container stage | `infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile` L137-L179 (`development`) | Installs `requirements-dev.txt`, self-verifies pytest/pytest-flask/coverage, copies `tests/` into the image |
| Verification pipeline | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (340 L) | `test`, `security` and `quality-gate` jobs |
| Post-deployment verification | `.github/workflows/cd.yml` L501-L861 | Health gates, six staging smoke tests, five production smoke tests, 6-minute stability watch |

Two absences are structural rather than incidental and are referenced throughout this section: there is **no `conftest.py` anywhere in the repository** (all fixtures are defined at the bottom of each test module), and there are **no fixture data files, factories, or seed scripts** — every input a test needs is either a literal in a parametrize table or generated in-process.

#### 6.6.1.3 Testing Layers Actually Implemented

| Layer | Implementing Assets | What It Proves |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | `test_app.py` classes `TestFlaskApplication`, `TestFlaskConfigurationManagement` | Application-factory behaviour and per-environment configuration without HTTP |
| API / integration (in-process) | `test_app.py` route, error-handler, security, middleware and statelessness classes | Full Flask request/response cycle through the test client |
| Integration (real server) | `test_wsgi.py` `TestWSGIServerLifecycle`, `TestFlaskWSGIIntegration` | Gunicorn actually loads the WSGI callable, binds a port, serves and shuts down |
| Performance / load | `test_app.py::TestFlaskPerformanceCharacteristics`, `test_wsgi.py::TestWSGIPerformance` | Latency, memory and concurrency thresholds under `pytest-benchmark`, `psutil` and `ThreadPoolExecutor` |
| End-to-end | `test_wsgi.py::TestWSGIEndToEndIntegration`, CD smoke suites | Four-phase deploy→validate→load→shutdown lifecycle locally; HTTP contract verification against deployed Azure Web Apps |
| Static / security analysis | `flake8` (blocking), `bandit`, `safety`, `pip-audit`, OSSF Scorecard, Trivy | Style/complexity, Python vulnerability patterns, dependency and image CVEs, supply-chain posture |

#### 6.6.1.4 Scope Boundaries with Other Specification Sections

| Concern | Owning Section | What 6.6 Adds |
|---|---|---|
| Tool inventory, versions, CI/CD job anatomy | 3.6 Development & Deployment | The testing view: which layer each job verifies and how failures are handled |
| Consolidated performance thresholds by enforcement layer | 5.4 Cross-Cutting Concerns (5.4.5) | Where each threshold is *asserted in a test* and with what tolerance |
| Runtime observability, probe cadences, artifact retention | 6.5 Monitoring and Observability | Test-time reporting artifacts and the reason production thresholds are unobserved |
| Security controls and hardening posture | 6.4 Security Architecture | Security **testing** requirements: scanners, gates, and in-suite security assertions |
| Component contracts and error envelopes | 5.2, 6.3 | The assertions that pin those contracts |

Sub-section 6.6.9 records verified defects in the test apparatus. Those findings are reported because they materially change what the strategy currently achieves: as committed, neither `pytest.ini` parses, so the suite documented in 6.6.2 through 6.6.4 cannot execute without repair. Every capability described in this section is documented as *implemented in the repository*, with its executable status stated where it differs.


### 6.6.2 Unit Testing

#### 6.6.2.1 Testing Frameworks and Tools

The unit-testing stack is pytest-centric and was introduced as a direct replacement for the pre-migration Jest suite — `test_app.py` states this in its module docstring: *"Replaces app.test.js Jest test suite with Python Flask testing patterns."* The tools below are declared across `requirements-dev.txt`, `src/backend/requirements.txt` and the `dev`/`performance` extras of `pyproject.toml`.

| Tool | Declared Constraint | Role in the Suite |
|---|---|---|
| pytest | `>=8.4.0` | Test runner, fixtures, parametrization, assertion rewriting |
| pytest-flask | `>=1.3.0` | Declared as a required plugin in all three configs; `pytest_plugins` in `test_wsgi.py` L1397 |
| pytest-cov | `>=5.0.0` (root) / `>=6.1.0` (backend `required_plugins`) | Branch-aware coverage collection and the `--cov-fail-under` gate |
| coverage[toml] | `>=7.6.0` | Measurement engine; configured by `[tool.coverage.*]` in `pyproject.toml` |
| pytest-benchmark | `>=4.0.0` | Statistical latency benchmarking (`benchmark.pedantic`, `benchmark.stats`) |
| psutil | `>=5.9.0` / `>=5.9.6` | RSS/VMS sampling for memory assertions |
| pytest-html | `>=4.1.0` / `>=4.1.1` | `--html=pytest_report.html --self-contained-html` reporting |
| pytest-xdist | `>=3.5.0` | Declared and documented for parallelism, **never invoked** (see 6.6.5.3) |
| pytest-mock | `>=3.12.0` | Declared in `src/backend/requirements.txt` and the `dev` extra; the `mocker` fixture is never used |
| requests | `>=2.31.0` | Real HTTP client for out-of-process integration tests |
| python-dotenv | `>=1.0.1` | `load_dotenv('.env.testing')` in the session fixture |

Two categories of tooling are declared but demonstrably unused by the suite. Verified by import search across both test modules: **`Faker`/`faker`, `factory-boy`, `freezegun`, `responses`, `vcrpy`, `jsonschema`, `pytest-mock`, `pytest-clarity` and `pytest-tmp-path` are never imported.** Separately, two ini options are used by all three pytest configurations without their providing plugins being declared anywhere: `timeout`/`timeout_method` require `pytest-timeout` (declared in no manifest) and `env` requires `pytest-env` (declared only in root `requirements-dev.txt` L221). Because every configuration also sets `--strict-config`, unknown ini options are escalated to errors rather than warnings.

#### 6.6.2.2 Test Organization Structure

Tests live in a single flat directory, `src/backend/tests/`, containing exactly two modules. Organization is by **test class**, which the suite adopts as the explicit替 replacement for Jest `describe()` blocks (`test_app.py` L59-L62 comments state this).

| Module | Test Classes | Tests | Focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_app.py` | 8 | 25 | Factory, routes, error handlers, security headers, performance, statelessness, middleware, configuration |
| `test_wsgi.py` | 5 | 11 | Server lifecycle, WSGI integration, performance, environment configuration, end-to-end lifecycle |

The eight classes in `test_app.py` are `TestFlaskApplication`, `TestFlaskRouteHandlers`, `TestFlaskErrorHandlers`, `TestFlaskSecurityConfiguration`, `TestFlaskPerformanceCharacteristics`, `TestFlaskStatelessOperation`, `TestFlaskMiddlewareIntegration` and `TestFlaskConfigurationManagement`. The five in `test_wsgi.py` are `TestWSGIServerLifecycle`, `TestFlaskWSGIIntegration`, `TestWSGIPerformance`, `TestWSGIEnvironmentConfiguration` and `TestWSGIEndToEndIntegration`.

Discovery is configured three times with slightly different patterns:

| Setting | `pytest.ini` (root) | `src/backend/pytest.ini` |
|---|---|---|
| `testpaths` | `src/backend/tests` | `tests` |
| `python_files` | `test_*.py`, `*_test.py` | `test_*.py` |
| `python_classes` | `Test*` | `Test*` |
| `python_functions` | `test_*` | `test_*` |

There is **no `conftest.py`**, so no fixture is shared between the two modules: `memory_monitor` is defined independently in both (`test_app.py` L675, `test_wsgi.py` L127) with different tolerances, and the module-level `pytest_plugins` declaration in `test_wsgi.py` L1397 has no effect because modern pytest honours that variable only in the rootdir `conftest.py`. Test modules also lack `__init__.py` (the repository contains none), so both modules are imported as top-level modules under pytest's default `prepend` import mode.

#### 6.6.2.3 Mocking Strategy

The suite deliberately minimises mocking: the system under test has no external dependency to stub, so tests exercise the real Flask application and, in `test_wsgi.py`, a real Gunicorn process. Three mechanisms are used.

| Mechanism | Where Used | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `unittest.mock.patch` / `MagicMock` | `test_app.py` L42 import; `patch('src.app.hello_route_handler', …)` L309 | Simulate a route raising `RuntimeError` to reach the 500 handler |
| pytest `monkeypatch` | `test_app.py` L654-L662 (autouse), L603-L609; `test_wsgi.py` L1009 | Set/restore `FLASK_ENV`, `TESTING`, `LOG_LEVEL` without leaking state |
| pytest `caplog` | `test_app.py` L528-L538 | Assert that middleware emits the expected INFO records |

Environment isolation is treated as the primary substitute for mocking. `test_wsgi.py` L85-L124 snapshots `os.environ`, applies a testing profile, and restores the original mapping on teardown; `test_app.py`'s autouse `setup_test_environment` fixture applies the same idea per test via `monkeypatch`. Process-level dependencies are not mocked at all — the WSGI suite launches `python -m gunicorn` through `subprocess.Popen` and drives it over real HTTP with `requests`.

The 500-handler test is the one place where the mocking approach does not hold together: `hello_route_handler` is a nested function defined inside `register_route_handlers` (`src/backend/app.py` L368), so it is not an attribute of the `src.app` module and cannot be patched at that path. The test's own comment acknowledges the workaround ("For now, we'll test the error handler directly") and reaches into `app.error_handler_spec` instead.

#### 6.6.2.4 Code Coverage Requirements

Coverage is the strictest gate in the repository: **100 % of both line and branch coverage**, enforced in four independent places.

| Enforcement Point | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Root `pytest.ini` addopts | `--cov=src/backend --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100`, plus `--cov-context=test`, `--no-cov-on-fail` |
| `src/backend/pytest.ini` addopts | `--cov=src --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` |
| `pyproject.toml` | `[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 100`, `precision = 2`, `show_missing = true`, `skip_covered = false` |
| CI quality gate | `COVERAGE_THRESHOLD: 100` and `scripts/validate_coverage.py`, which fails when **either** `line-rate` or `branch-rate` is below the threshold |

Measurement scope comes from `[tool.coverage.run]`: `source = ["src"]`, `branch = true`, with `omit` covering `tests/*`, `*/conftest.py`, `*/test_*.py`, `venv/*`, `.venv/*`, `build/*`, `dist/*`. Exclusion regexes in `[tool.coverage.report]` are the conventional set — `pragma: no cover`, `def __repr__`, `if self.debug:`, `if settings.DEBUG`, `raise AssertionError`, `raise NotImplementedError`, `if 0:`, `if __name__ == .__main__.:`, `class .*\bProtocol\):`, `@(abc\.)?abstractmethod`. The same list is duplicated as an unrecognised `exclude_lines` key in `src/backend/pytest.ini`.

Four report formats are produced on every run: `term-missing`, `html:htmlcov`, `xml:coverage.xml` and `json:coverage.json` (titled "Flask Migration Tutorial - Coverage Report" for HTML). Root `pytest.ini` additionally passes `--cov-config=.coveragerc`, but **no `.coveragerc` file exists** at the repository root or under `src/backend`, so the configured coverage settings would not be loaded from the referenced path.

#### 6.6.2.5 Test Naming Conventions

Naming is consistent and behaviour-oriented across both modules; conventions are enforced by discovery patterns rather than by a linter.

| Convention | Rule Observed | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Module | `test_<subject>.py` | `test_app.py`, `test_wsgi.py` |
| Class | `Test<Subject><Aspect>` | `TestFlaskErrorHandlers`, `TestWSGIPerformance` |
| Function | `test_<subject>_<expected behaviour>` | `test_unsupported_method_returns_405_with_json_error` |
| Documentation | Every test carries a docstring | 25/25 in `test_app.py`, 11/11 in `test_wsgi.py` (verified) |

Test-function names range from 23 to 51 characters and encode the assertion in the name, so a JUnit report reads as a specification. Markers form a second, less disciplined naming layer: the configurations declare **18 markers** in root `pytest.ini`, **10** in `src/backend/pytest.ini` and **10** in `pyproject.toml`, but only five are ever applied — `unit` and `flask` at `test_app.py` L694 and `wsgi`, `integration`, `performance` at `test_wsgi.py` L1390 — plus `parametrize` (×3) and `benchmark` (×2) inline. Consequently the marker-based selection documented in `src/backend/README.md` (`pytest -m unit`, `-m integration`, `-m performance`) selects whole modules rather than individual tests, and `-m security`, `-m health`, `-m smoke` or `-m e2e` would select nothing.

#### 6.6.2.6 Test Data Management

There is no test-data layer to manage in the conventional sense: the application stores nothing, so no dataset, factory, seed script or fixture file exists anywhere in the repository. All test input is produced by one of four in-process mechanisms.

| Data Class | Source | Lifecycle |
|---|---|---|
| Endpoint/status vectors | `@pytest.mark.parametrize` literal tables (`test_app.py` L217-L221, L318-L322) | Per test invocation |
| Configuration data | `env` blocks in the pytest configs plus `monkeypatch.setenv` in fixtures | Restored on teardown |
| Network resources | `dynamic_port` fixture — `socket.bind(('localhost', 0))`, asserted within 1024-65535 (`test_wsgi.py` L194-L231) | Released, and `FLASK_RUN_PORT`/`WSGI_PORT` popped, on teardown |
| Measurement baselines | `psutil` RSS snapshots and `performance_baseline` threshold dictionaries | Per test / per fixture |

Expected values are asserted as literals: `data['message'] == 'Hello world'`, `data['status'] == 'success'`, `X-API-Version == '1.0'`, `X-Content-Type-Options == 'nosniff'`, `X-Frame-Options == 'DENY'`. The declared data-generation libraries (`Faker`, `factory-boy`, `freezegun`) are unused, and `src/backend/README.md` L593-L597 documents a `tests/conftest.py` with "Mock data generators using Faker library" that does not exist. One environment artifact is also referenced but absent: `test_wsgi.py` L101 calls `load_dotenv('.env.testing', override=True)` and the repository contains no `.env.testing` (only `src/backend/.env.example`); `python-dotenv` silently no-ops on a missing file, so the fixture's explicit `os.environ.update` block supplies the effective values.

#### 6.6.2.7 Example Test Patterns

The four canonical patterns in the suite, each shown at minimum length.

Route contract assertion through the Flask test client:

```python
response = client.get('/hello')
assert response.status_code == 200 and response.is_json
assert response.get_json()['message'] == 'Hello world'
```

Parametric coverage of multiple endpoints in one function:

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("endpoint,expected_status", [("/hello", 200), ("/health", 200)])
def test_valid_endpoints_parametric_testing(self, client, endpoint, expected_status):
    assert client.get(endpoint).status_code == expected_status
```

Threshold assertion with a diagnostic failure message:

```python
response_time = (time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000
assert response_time < 50.0, f"Response time {response_time:.2f}ms exceeds 50ms SLA"
```

Fixture-based resource guard that validates after the test body completes:

```python
yield baseline_memory
assert memory_growth < 10.0, f"Memory growth {memory_growth:.2f}MB exceeds 10MB limit per test"
```

Note that the term "SLA" in these messages is an assertion label only; as 6.5.2.4 records, the repository defines no service-level agreement.


### 6.6.3 Integration Testing

#### 6.6.3.1 Service Integration Test Approach

Integration testing operates at two distinct levels, and the distinction matters because only one of them exercises the production serving path.

| Level | Mechanism | Serving Path Exercised |
|---|---|---|
| In-process integration | Flask test client from the `client` fixture (`test_app.py` L635-L641) | Werkzeug test request context; no socket, no WSGI server |
| Out-of-process integration | `subprocess.Popen(['python', '-m', 'gunicorn', …])` + `requests` (`test_wsgi.py`) | Real Gunicorn arbiter, real worker processes, real TCP socket |

The out-of-process approach is the repository's substitute for service-to-service integration testing. Five tests launch Gunicorn against `src.backend.wsgi:application` on a fixture-allocated ephemeral port and drive it over loopback HTTP:

| Test | Server Configuration | Integration Behaviour Verified |
|---|---|---|
| `test_wsgi_server_startup_lifecycle` (L362) | 1 worker, `--worker-class sync`, `--timeout 30`, access/error logs to stdout | Arbiter starts, `/health` answers 200 with `status == 'healthy'`, process still alive, memory within limit |
| `test_wsgi_server_signal_handling` (L458) | 1 worker | `SIGTERM` triggers graceful exit in under 10 s; port stops answering (`pytest.raises(RequestException)`) |
| `test_wsgi_server_port_binding_validation` (L530) | temporary port | Binding succeeds on the allocated port and cleanup force-kills on timeout |
| `test_wsgi_server_memory_usage_validation` (L788) | server + 50 requests | RSS growth under 20 MB across a request batch |
| `test_wsgi_server_concurrent_load_testing` (L865) | 2 workers | 100 requests via `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10)`; ≥ 95 % success rate and < 50 ms average |

Readiness is established by polling rather than by fixed sleeps: the startup test retries `GET /health` once per second for up to 10 s and calls `pytest.fail` if the loop is exhausted (L404-L420), and the module also provides a reusable `wait_for_server_readiness(host, port, timeout=30)` helper at L1327. Every server-launching test wraps its assertions in `try/finally` with `process.terminate()`, a 5-second `process.wait(timeout=5)`, and `process.kill()` on `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` — so a hung server cannot leak into subsequent tests.

#### 6.6.3.2 API Testing Strategy

The API surface is two routes plus the error envelopes, and the suite pins the full contract of each. Assertions are grouped by contract element below; all are drawn from `test_app.py` unless noted.

| Contract Element | Asserted Expectation | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `/hello` success | HTTP 200, `is_json`, `content_type == 'application/json'`, keys `message`/`timestamp`/`status`, `message == 'Hello world'`, ISO-8601 timestamp parses | L111-L141 |
| `/health` success | HTTP 200, JSON with `status == 'healthy'`, `timestamp`, `uptime`, `version`, `environment`; `Cache-Control` contains `no-cache` | L191-L215 |
| Versioning header | `X-API-Version == '1.0'` present on `/hello` | L143-L165 |
| Unknown route | HTTP 404, JSON error envelope with `status` and `error == 'Not Found'` | L237-L265, L318-L340 |
| Wrong method | HTTP 405, JSON envelope, `Allow` header contains `GET` and not `POST` | L267-L293 |
| Server error | 500 handler resolved from `app.error_handler_spec` returns status 500 | L295-L316 |
| Statelessness | Repeated requests return identical payloads; no session cookie is set | L482-L521 |
| Middleware effects | `X-Response-Time` present and numeric; `X-Request-ID` present with `req_` prefix; INFO log records emitted | L528-L575 |

The out-of-process suite re-verifies the same contracts over real HTTP and adds a shared validator, `validate_wsgi_response_format(response, expected_keys)` (`test_wsgi.py` L1357), which asserts status 200, JSON content and the presence of each expected key. The end-to-end lifecycle test drives a table of endpoint expectations — `[('/health', 200, 'status'), ('/hello', 200, 'message')]` — through the running server.

No contract-testing tooling (OpenAPI schema validation, Pact, `jsonschema`) is used; `jsonschema>=4.20.0` is declared in `src/backend/requirements.txt` and `requirements-dev.txt` but never imported. Response shape is therefore asserted key-by-key in Python.

#### 6.6.3.3 Database Integration Testing

**Not applicable.** The system has no database, ORM, migration tool, cache or persistent store of any kind: no database driver appears in `requirements.txt`, `requirements-dev.txt` or `src/backend/requirements.txt`; no datastore service exists in `infrastructure/docker/docker-compose.yml`; and the application holds no state beyond the current request (a property the suite asserts explicitly in `TestFlaskStatelessOperation`). Section 6.2 Database Design records the same determination for the persistence layer.

The only trace of database testing in the repository is aspirational documentation: `src/backend/README.md` L593-L597 lists "Database fixtures (if implemented in future)" among the contents of a `tests/conftest.py` that does not exist. No test setup, teardown, transaction rollback, or schema-migration verification is required or present.

#### 6.6.3.4 External Service Mocking

At runtime the application calls nothing outbound — the two runtime modules import no HTTP client, RPC stub or socket helper — so there is no external service to mock for functional tests. The suite reflects this: HTTP-record/replay and stubbing libraries are declared and unused (`responses>=0.24.0` and `vcrpy>=6.0.0` in `requirements-dev.txt`), and the only network traffic any test generates is loopback traffic to a Gunicorn process the test itself started.

| Potential External Dependency | Present at Runtime? | Test Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Datastore / cache / broker | No | Nothing to mock |
| Downstream HTTP API | No | Nothing to mock |
| Gunicorn WSGI server | Yes, in production | **Not mocked** — launched as a real subprocess |
| Container runtime | Yes, in deployment | Not exercised by pytest; `docker` marker declared but unused, `docker>=7.0.0` SDK declared and unimported |
| CI/CD services (Codecov, GHCR, Azure, Trivy) | Pipeline-only | Not mocked; exercised live by the workflows |

#### 6.6.3.5 Test Environment Management

Environment management is fixture-driven and, for the WSGI suite, session-scoped.

| Concern | Implementation | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline test configuration | `env` blocks in all three pytest configs set `FLASK_ENV=testing`, `TESTING=1`, `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED=False`, `LOG_LEVEL=ERROR` (root adds `SECRET_KEY=testing-secret-key-not-for-production`) | Whole session |
| Environment snapshot/restore | `configure_wsgi_test_environment` copies `os.environ`, applies the testing profile, then clears and restores it (`test_wsgi.py` L85-L124) | `session`, autouse |
| Per-test environment | `setup_test_environment` uses `monkeypatch.setenv` and times the test, warning above 1 000 ms (`test_app.py` L653-L670) | Function, autouse |
| Application instance | `create_testing_app()` / `create_app(config_name='testing')`, then `TESTING=True`, `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED=False`, `SECRET_KEY='test-secret-key'` overrides | Function |
| Port isolation | `dynamic_port` ephemeral allocation; `FLASK_RUN_PORT`/`WSGI_PORT` exported and popped | Function |
| Hard time limits | `timeout = 300`, `timeout_method = thread` in all three configs | Per test |

The application cooperates with this design: `create_app` has an explicit `testing` branch that sets `DEBUG=False`, `TESTING=True` and `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED=False` (`src/backend/app.py` L195-L204), and `create_testing_app()` (L682-L690) is the factory the fixtures call. A separate module-level `FLASK_CONFIGS` map (L641-L657) declares a `testing` profile with `LOG_LEVEL: 'WARNING'` but is not read by any code path.

Two environment facilities exist outside pytest. The container `development` stage is a self-verifying test image — it installs `requirements-dev.txt` and fails the build unless `pytest`, `pytest_flask` and `coverage` all import (`infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile` L145-L155) — and `docker-compose.yml` L14 documents the containerized invocation `docker-compose run --rm flask-tutorial-dev python -m pytest`. In CI, the environment is provided by `actions/setup-python@v4` across three interpreter versions with pip caching, and workflow-level `env` sets `FLASK_ENV=testing`, `CI=true` and `COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=100`. `src/backend/pytest.ini` additionally declares `integration_timeout = 60`, `integration_retries = 3`, `integration_delay = 1`, `container_testing = true` and `health_check_timeout = 30`, but these are not pytest ini options and have no effect on execution; the operative timeouts are the ones in the table above and the in-test polling loops.


### 6.6.4 End-to-End Testing

#### 6.6.4.1 End-to-End Test Scenarios

End-to-end coverage exists in two forms: one pytest scenario that exercises a complete local deployment lifecycle, and two shell-based suites that verify the deployed application over the public internet. There is no third-party E2E framework (no Playwright, Cypress, Selenium or Robot Framework) in any manifest.

The pytest scenario is `test_wsgi.py::TestWSGIEndToEndIntegration::test_complete_wsgi_deployment_lifecycle` (L1125-L1325). It runs Gunicorn with a production-like command line — `--workers 2 --timeout 30 --worker-class sync --max-requests 1000 --preload-app` against `src.backend.wsgi:application` — and records the duration of four named phases:

| Phase | Actions | Assertions |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Startup | Launch Gunicorn, poll `/health` for up to 15 s | `server_ready` must be true or the test fails |
| 2 — Validation | Request `('/health', 200, 'status')` and `('/hello', 200, 'message')` | Status code matches and the expected JSON key is present |
| 3 — Load testing | Sustained load: 10 s at 10 requests/second (100 requests) | Success rate ≥ 95 %; average response time < 100 ms |
| 4 — Shutdown | `process.terminate()`, wait up to 10 s | Exit code 0; force-kill on timeout |

After the phases complete, the test asserts a whole-lifecycle budget — `total_lifecycle_duration < 60` seconds (L1309) — and re-validates memory through the `memory_monitor` fixture.

The deployment-time E2E suites live in `.github/workflows/cd.yml` and are pure `curl`/`bc` shell steps; `pytest` is never invoked in the CD pipeline. Their scenario coverage is:

| Suite | Target | Scenarios |
|---|---|---|
| Staging smoke tests (L536-L599) | `flask-tutorial-staging.azurewebsites.net` | Body contains "Hello world"; HTTP 200; `Content-Type` contains `application/json`; single-request latency < 3.0 s (warning only); `/health` returns 200; `/nonexistent` returns 404 |
| Production smoke tests (L757-L820) | `flask-tutorial.azurewebsites.net` | `/hello` body check; 10-request average latency < 1.5 s (warning only); 15 parallel background requests (no assertion); `/nonexistent` returns 404; `/health` body contains "healthy" |
| Post-deploy stability watch (L824-L861) | Production | 12 checks at 30 s intervals; sets `rollback_required=true` and fails when the running failure rate exceeds 20 % |

Both suites are preceded by a retry-based readiness gate — 12 attempts with 20 s back-off for staging, 18 attempts with 25 s back-off plus a body match for production — and by fixed warm-up sleeps of 45 s and 75 s respectively.

#### 6.6.4.2 UI Automation Approach

**Not applicable.** The system has no user interface to automate: both routes return `application/json`, the application registers no template directory or static folder, and no templating, asset-pipeline, or browser-automation dependency appears in any manifest. Section 7 of this specification records the same determination for the user-interface layer, and the repository's retained pre-migration specification reaches it too ("No user interface required").

The nearest equivalent to UI automation is HTTP-client automation: the Flask test client for in-process assertions, `requests` for loopback assertions against Gunicorn, and `curl` for assertions against the deployed Azure Web Apps.

#### 6.6.4.3 Test Data Setup and Teardown

E2E flows manage infrastructure rather than data, because no data outlives a request. Setup and teardown responsibilities are therefore process- and environment-scoped.

| Stage | Setup | Teardown |
|---|---|---|
| Session | `configure_wsgi_test_environment` snapshots `os.environ`, loads `.env.testing` if present, applies the testing profile | Clears and restores the original environment mapping |
| Per test | `dynamic_port` allocates an ephemeral port and exports `FLASK_RUN_PORT`/`WSGI_PORT`; `memory_monitor` records an RSS baseline | Pops both variables; asserts memory growth bounds |
| Server | `subprocess.Popen` launches Gunicorn; readiness confirmed by polling `/health` | `try/finally` with `terminate()` → `wait(timeout=5)` → `kill()`; the lifecycle test additionally asserts exit code 0 |
| Deployed environment | `azure/webapps-deploy@v2` publishes the digest-pinned image; fixed warm-up sleep | None — the deployment is left running; verification is read-only |

Because every deployed-environment check is a `GET` against `/hello`, `/health` or a deliberately non-existent path, the E2E suites create no state and require no cleanup or data reset. The one teardown risk the suite guards against explicitly is an orphaned Gunicorn process, which is why every server-launching test uses the terminate-then-kill pattern.

#### 6.6.4.4 Performance Testing Requirements

Performance testing is a first-class part of the suite rather than a separate exercise, implemented with `pytest-benchmark` for statistical latency, `psutil` for memory, and `ThreadPoolExecutor` for concurrency.

| Requirement | Threshold Asserted | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Warm request latency (test client) | < 50 ms per request | `test_app.py` L184 |
| Benchmark mean latency (real Gunicorn) | mean < 50 ms over 10 iterations × 3 rounds | `test_wsgi.py` L717-L768 |
| Latency under in-process concurrency | average < 50 ms, maximum < 100 ms across 50 requests | `test_app.py` L454-L455 |
| Latency under server concurrency | average < 50 ms across 100 requests, 10 threads | `test_wsgi.py` L960 |
| Sustained-load latency (E2E) | average < 100 ms over 10 s at 10 req/s | `test_wsgi.py` Phase 3 |
| Request success rate under load | 50/50 in-process; ≥ 95 % against Gunicorn | `test_app.py` L447; `test_wsgi.py` L954, L1258 |
| Resident memory | < 75 MB total | `test_app.py` L426; `test_wsgi.py` L148, L189 |
| Memory growth | < 5 MB per request batch, < 10 MB per test, < 20 MB in WSGI load test | `test_app.py` L427, L690; `test_wsgi.py` L188, L843 |
| Cold start | `cold_start_ms = 100` threshold in the `performance_baseline` fixture | `test_wsgi.py` L307-L311 |
| Graceful shutdown | < 10 s, exit code 0 | `test_wsgi.py` L511, Phase 4 |
| Whole-lifecycle budget | < 60 s | `test_wsgi.py` L1309 |
| Slow-test warning | Warns when a single test exceeds 1 000 ms | `test_app.py` L668-L670 |

Benchmark behaviour is configured declaratively in `pyproject.toml`: `[tool.pytest.ini_options.benchmark]` and `[tool.pytest-benchmark]` set `min_time = 0.001`, `max_time = 1.0`, `min_rounds = 3`, `timer = "time.perf_counter"`, `disable_gc = false`, `warmup = false`, `sort = "mean"`, `histogram = true` and `json_output = "benchmark_results.json"`; `src/backend/pytest.ini` repeats `benchmark_min_rounds = 3` and `benchmark_warmup = false` as non-standard keys. Two consequences follow from the evidence. First, no workflow uploads `benchmark_results.json` and no run passes `--benchmark-autosave` or `--benchmark-compare`, so the `performance_regression_threshold = 10` declared in `[tool.quality-gates]` has no stored baseline and is never evaluated — 6.5.2.2 records the same finding. Second, every sub-50 ms threshold is measured either through the Flask test client or against a loopback Gunicorn process, never through the Azure platform edge, which is why the deployment-time checks are expressed in seconds (3.0 s and 1.5 s) and are warning-only.

Documented-but-unimplemented performance tooling should not be mistaken for capability: `docker-compose.yml` L531 suggests `ab -n 1000 -c 10 http://localhost:3000/hello`, yet Apache Bench is not installed by the Dockerfile or declared in any manifest, and `memory-profiler>=0.61.0` and `line-profiler>=4.1.0` (root `requirements-dev.txt`) are never imported by a test.

#### 6.6.4.5 Cross-Browser Testing Strategy

**Not applicable.** With no HTML, CSS or JavaScript delivered by the application, browser rendering differences cannot arise; the only client-side variability that matters is HTTP client behaviour, which the suite covers through three different clients (Werkzeug test client, `requests`, `curl`). No browser matrix, browser-automation dependency, device-emulation configuration or visual-regression tooling exists in the repository, and none is required by the two JSON endpoints. Client compatibility is instead asserted at the protocol level: media type, status code, header presence and JSON key structure, as documented in 6.6.3.2.


### 6.6.5 Test Automation

#### 6.6.5.1 CI/CD Integration

Test automation is implemented entirely with GitHub Actions. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is the verification pipeline and `.github/workflows/cd.yml` performs post-deployment verification; section 3.6 documents the full job anatomy, so the description below is limited to the testing behaviour of each job.

| Job | Testing Responsibility | Blocking Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `test` (ci.yml, 15 min) | `flake8 . --config=.flake8 --statistics --count` then `pytest --cov=src … --cov-fail-under=100 --junit-xml=junit.xml --html=pytest_report.html --self-contained-html -v` | Lint or test failure fails the matrix leg |
| `security` (ci.yml, 10 min) | Bandit, Safety, pip-audit, OSSF Scorecard (see 6.6.7) | Report generation is non-blocking (`|| true`); the bare enforcement invocations block |
| `quality-gate` (ci.yml, 10 min) | `needs: [test, security]`; re-validates coverage from `coverage.xml` and re-checks security findings | Fails the workflow when either coverage rate is below 100 % or a HIGH Bandit / any Safety finding exists |
| `deploy_staging` / `deploy_production` (cd.yml) | Retry-based health gates plus `curl`-based smoke suites | Contract checks exit 1; latency checks only warn |
| `deployment_notification` (cd.yml, `if: always()`) | Aggregates job outcomes into `deployment-report.md` | Never blocks |

Both test-executing steps run with `working-directory: src/backend`, which is the origin of two of the defects recorded in 6.6.9: the step installs root-level `requirements-dev.txt` from a directory that does not contain it, and `--cov=src` names a path that does not exist below `src/backend`.

#### 6.6.5.2 Automated Test Triggers

| Trigger | Definition | Scope of Automation |
|---|---|---|
| `push` to `main`/`develop` | Path-filtered on `src/backend/**`, `tests/**`, `requirements.txt`, `requirements-dev.txt`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml` | Full CI pipeline |
| `pull_request` to `main` | Types `opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened` | Full CI pipeline on every push to the PR branch |
| `schedule` | Cron `0 2 * * 1` (Mondays, 02:00 UTC) | Full CI pipeline as a weekly dependency and security sweep |
| `workflow_dispatch` | Manual, no inputs | Full CI pipeline on demand |
| `workflow_run` | Workflows `["CI Pipeline"]`, types `[completed]`, branches `[main]` | CD pipeline, gated on CI success |
| `release` published / manual dispatch | `environment` choice, `image_tag`, `skip_tests` | CD pipeline including its smoke suites |

Concurrency policy differs deliberately between the two pipelines: CI uses `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a new push supersedes an in-flight test run; CD uses `cd-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a deployment and its verification are never interrupted. Note also that the `skip_tests` dispatch input, despite its name, gates only the CD `security_scan` job — its description reads "Skip security scanning for emergency deployments" — and the path filter omits `.flake8`, `.github/workflows/**` and `infrastructure/**`, so changes to the lint policy, the pipelines themselves, or the container assets do not trigger a push-based run.

#### 6.6.5.3 Parallel Test Execution

Parallelism exists at the job level only.

| Dimension | Configuration | Effective Parallelism |
|---|---|---|
| Interpreter matrix | `strategy.matrix.python-version: ['3.12','3.11','3.10']` | Three concurrent, independent full test runs |
| Independent jobs | `test` and `security` have no `needs` relationship | Run concurrently; `quality-gate` waits for both |
| Within-suite distribution | `pytest-xdist>=3.5.0` declared as a required plugin; `pytest.ini` L140 documents "Usage: pytest -n auto"; `src/backend/pytest.ini` declares `max_workers = auto` and `distributed_testing = true` | **None** — no workflow, addopts entry, or documented command passes `-n` |
| In-test concurrency | `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10)` inside individual tests | Concurrency is the subject under test, not a scheduling strategy |

The matrix also conflicts with the project's own floor: `pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, yet two of the three matrix legs run 3.11 and 3.10. Enabling `-n auto` would additionally require care in this suite, because several tests bind sockets, spawn Gunicorn processes and assert on process-wide `psutil` RSS — measurements that are not isolated between xdist workers.

#### 6.6.5.4 Test Reporting Requirements

Every run emits five machine- or human-readable outputs, and CI archives them as artifacts.

| Output | Produced By | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `coverage.xml` | `--cov-report=xml:coverage.xml` | Codecov upload and the `quality-gate` validator |
| `coverage.json`, `htmlcov/` | `--cov-report=json` / `html:htmlcov` | Programmatic analysis and human browsing |
| `junit.xml` | `--junit-xml=junit.xml` with `junit_family = xunit2`, `junit_logging = all`, `junit_log_passing_tests = true`, `junit_duration_report = total` | GitHub test-result visualisation |
| `pytest_report.html` | `--html=… --self-contained-html` (title "Flask Migration Tutorial - Test Results") | Shareable single-file report |
| `tests.log` / `logs/pytest.log` | `log_file` at DEBUG in the two pytest configs | Local debugging only — **never uploaded** |

Artifact retention is 30 days for `coverage-reports-python-<version>` and `test-results-python-<version>`, and 90 days for `security-reports`; the test-results upload carries `if: always()` so reports survive a failing run, whereas the coverage-artifact upload does not. Coverage is also pushed to Codecov with `flags: unittests` and `fail_ci_if_error: false`, making Codecov the only cross-run trend surface (6.5.1.1). Console reporting is configured for readability rather than terseness: `--verbose`, `--tb=short`, `console_output_style = progress`, `showlocals = true`, and live logging at INFO with a timestamped format.

#### 6.6.5.5 Failed Test Handling

Failure handling is intentionally two-tier — contract failures block, timing observations warn.

| Failure Class | Handling | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Test assertion failure | pytest exits non-zero; `--no-cov-on-fail` suppresses a misleading coverage report | Matrix leg fails; `quality-gate` never runs |
| Coverage below 100 % | `--cov-fail-under=100`, then the `quality-gate` XML check | Workflow fails |
| Lint failure | `flake8` exits non-zero before pytest runs | Tests do not execute for that leg |
| Security report generation | `|| true` on the JSON/SARIF invocations | Never blocks; artifacts still uploaded |
| Security enforcement runs | Bare `bandit -r src/ --severity-level medium`, `safety check --short-report`, `pip-audit` | Block the `security` job |
| Missing security report in the gate | `if [ -f … ]` guard prints "⚠️ … skipping" | Gate passes without validating |
| Deployment contract check | `exit 1` inside the `curl` step | Deployment job fails, promotion blocked |
| Deployment latency check | `echo "⚠️ …"` only | Deployment proceeds |
| Server never becomes ready (tests) | `pytest.fail(...)` after the polling loop | Test fails, process still force-killed in `finally` |

No fail-fast or bail-out policy is active: `pytest.ini` L215-L218 contains `--exitfirst` and `--maxfail=10` as commented-out suggestions, and no workflow step uses `continue-on-error`, so each matrix leg runs its full suite and reports every failure. Local `pytest -x` is documented in `src/backend/README.md` for developer iteration only.

#### 6.6.5.6 Flaky Test Management

There is **no automated flaky-test management**: no `pytest-rerunfailures`, `flaky` or retry plugin is declared in any manifest, no test is retried, and no quarantine list or flake-detection job exists. Management is declarative and manual — root `pytest.ini` L108 declares a marker for the purpose, described as "Tests marked as potentially unstable requiring investigation", but no test carries it.

What the suite does contain is a set of structural flakiness risks that follow directly from its design, together with the mitigations that are present:

| Flakiness Source | Evidence | Mitigation Present |
|---|---|---|
| Wall-clock latency assertions on shared CI runners | `< 50 ms` and `< 100 ms` assertions on unfixed hardware | None; thresholds are absolute, not relative to a baseline |
| Absolute process-memory assertions | `assert current_memory < 75.0` measures whole-interpreter RSS, which includes pytest, plugins and coverage instrumentation | Growth-based assertions alongside absolute ones |
| Real subprocess startup timing | Gunicorn readiness polling and one `time.sleep(4)` before the concurrent-load test | Polling loops with 10-15 s budgets; force-kill cleanup |
| Ephemeral port reuse | `socket.bind(('localhost', 0))` then bind again from Gunicorn | Fresh port per test; range assertion |
| Cross-test process state | Module-scoped and session-scoped environment mutation | Environment snapshot/restore; `monkeypatch` per test |
| Deployed-environment probes | Public HTTPS calls to Azure Web Apps | Retry loops (12 and 18 attempts) and warning-only latency checks |

The deployment pipeline is the only place where retry is used as an anti-flake mechanism, and it retries *readiness*, not assertions: 12 attempts with 20 s back-off in staging, 18 attempts with 25 s back-off in production, plus fixed warm-up sleeps of 45 s and 75 s. The post-deploy stability watch is the inverse case — it computes a running failure rate over 12 checks with no minimum-sample guard, so a single early failure yields 100 % and trips the rollback flag immediately (a sensitivity 6.5.1.5 records in detail).

#### 6.6.5.7 Test Execution Flow

**Diagram 6.6.5-A — Test execution flow: from a developer change through the three CI jobs to the deployment-time verification suites, showing every blocking gate and the artifacts each stage produces.**


### 6.6.6 Quality Metrics

#### 6.6.6.1 Code Coverage Targets

The target is 100 % with no tolerance, applied to line **and** branch coverage. `README.md` L419-L424 states the same four metrics — line, function, branch and statement coverage at 100 % — and `src/backend/README.md` L450-L455 repeats them.

| Metric | Target | Enforcement Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Line coverage | 100 % | `--cov-fail-under=100`; `fail_under = 100`; `validate_coverage.py` `line-rate` check |
| Branch coverage | 100 % | `--cov-branch` plus the same three gates; the CI validator checks `branch-rate` separately |
| Function / statement coverage | 100 % (documented) | Not separately measured — `coverage.py` reports line and branch rates only |
| Measured scope | `src` (`[tool.coverage.run] source = ["src"]`), tests omitted | `omit` excludes `tests/*`, `*/conftest.py`, `*/test_*.py`, virtualenvs, `build/*`, `dist/*` |

A conflicting, lower target survives in the governance documents and should be read as pre-migration residue: `CONTRIBUTING.md` L1019 requires "Coverage minimum threshold (95%) enforced", its Jest configuration sample sets global thresholds of 95/100/95/95, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` L218 asks reviewers to confirm "Coverage meets minimum 95% threshold (100% target)", and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md` L131 repeats "100 % code coverage target (95 % minimum)". The executable configuration recognises no 95 % path — any run below 100 % fails.

#### 6.6.6.2 Test Success Rate Requirements

| Requirement | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Unit/integration suite pass rate | 100 % — any failing test fails the pipeline | `pytest` exit code; `quality-gate` depends on `test` |
| In-process concurrent requests | 50 of 50 must succeed | `test_app.py` L447 |
| Gunicorn load-test success rate | ≥ 95 % | `test_wsgi.py` L954, L1258 |
| Deployment smoke checks | All contract checks must pass (latency checks warn) | `.github/workflows/cd.yml` staging and production suites |
| Post-deployment stability | Running failure rate must stay ≤ 20 % over 12 checks | `.github/workflows/cd.yml` L847-L855 |
| Documented gate | "100 % test pass rate achieved" | `CONTRIBUTING.md` L1018 |

The asymmetry between the two load thresholds is deliberate in effect if not in intent: the in-process test tolerates no failures because it never crosses a socket, while both real-server load tests tolerate up to 5 % failures because they contend for ports, workers and CPU on the host.

#### 6.6.6.3 Performance Test Thresholds

The consolidated threshold set is reproduced here from the testing perspective — which layer enforces each threshold and whether the failure is blocking. Section 5.4.5 owns the cross-cutting view and 6.5.2.2 records which of these are observable in production (none of the sub-50 ms ones are).

| Threshold | Value | Enforcement Layer / Severity |
|---|---|---|
| Warm request latency | < 50 ms | pytest assertion — blocking |
| Benchmark mean latency | < 50 ms | pytest-benchmark assertion — blocking |
| Max latency under concurrency | < 100 ms | pytest assertion — blocking |
| Sustained-load average (E2E) | < 100 ms | pytest assertion — blocking |
| Cold start | < 100 ms (`cold_start_ms`) | `performance_baseline` fixture validator — blocking |
| Resident memory | < 75 MB | pytest assertion + `wsgi.py` runtime WARNING — blocking in tests only |
| Memory growth | < 5 MB / < 10 MB / < 20 MB by context | pytest assertions — blocking |
| Graceful shutdown | < 10 s, exit code 0 | pytest assertion — blocking |
| Whole lifecycle | < 60 s | pytest assertion — blocking |
| Staging single-request latency | < 3.0 s | CD `curl` check — warning only |
| Production 10-request average | < 1.5 s | CD `curl` check — warning only |
| Declared response-time limit | 50 ms (`response_time_limit_ms`) | `[tool.quality-gates]` — declarative, never read by a tool |
| Declared regression budget | 10 % (`performance_regression_threshold`) | Declarative; no baseline is persisted, so never evaluated |

#### 6.6.6.4 Quality Gates

Gates fall into two populations, and the distinction is the single most useful fact in this sub-section: a set of gates that actually run, and a set that is only declared.

| Executable Gate | Trigger Point | Failure Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `flake8` (88-char lines, complexity ≤ 10, `E,W,F,C,S,N,I` codes) | Before pytest in every matrix leg | Matrix leg fails |
| Full test suite pass | `test` job, three interpreter versions | Matrix leg fails |
| 100 % line + branch coverage | `--cov-fail-under=100`, re-validated in `quality-gate` | Workflow fails |
| Bandit at `--severity-level medium` | `security` job | Job fails |
| Safety and pip-audit enforcement runs | `security` job | Job fails |
| Zero HIGH Bandit findings / zero Safety vulnerabilities | `quality-gate` job | Workflow fails |
| Trivy CRITICAL findings on the image | CD `security_scan` | Deployment blocked |
| Staging and production contract smoke checks | CD deploy jobs | Deployment fails, promotion blocked |
| Post-deploy failure rate ≤ 20 % | CD monitoring step | Sets `rollback_required`, job fails |

| Declared-Only Gate | Declaration Site | Why It Does Not Execute |
|---|---|---|
| `quality_gate_coverage = 100`, `quality_gate_tests = 100`, `quality_gate_performance = true` | `src/backend/pytest.ini` L209-L212 | Non-standard ini keys; pytest does not interpret them |
| `coverage_threshold`, `memory_limit_mb`, `response_time_limit_ms`, `security_scan_required` | `pyproject.toml` `[tool.quality-gates]` | No tool reads this table |
| `vulnerability_threshold = 0`, `security_report_format = json` | `src/backend/pytest.ini` L241-L243 | Same |
| `archive_results`, `archive_retention_days = 30` | `src/backend/pytest.ini` L264-L266 | Retention actually comes from workflow artifacts |
| `black`, `isort`, `mypy`, `pylint`, `pydocstyle`, `pre-commit` | Manifests and `pyproject.toml` | No workflow step invokes them; no `.pre-commit-config.yaml` exists |

One executable gate has a documented soft spot worth recording: the `quality-gate` security validation is wrapped in `if [ -f … ]` guards, so if an upstream artifact is missing the step prints a warning and passes. Coverage validation has no such escape — the validator exits 1 when `coverage.xml` is absent.

#### 6.6.6.5 Documentation Requirements

Test documentation obligations are met inside the code and stated in the contribution templates.

| Requirement | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Every test documents its intent | Met — 36/36 test functions carry docstrings | Verified across both modules |
| Configuration documents its rationale | Met — both `pytest.ini` files are majority comment, cross-referencing spec sub-sections (for example "Section 6.6.4.1") | `pytest.ini`, `src/backend/pytest.ini` |
| Runbook-style test commands published | Met | `README.md` "Testing" section; `src/backend/README.md` L399-L513; `docker-compose.yml` header comments |
| PR must report coverage and test types | Required by template | `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` L209-L261 |
| Bug reports must include test output | Required by template | `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md` — `pytest tests/ --cov=src/backend --cov-report=term-missing -v` sample and "Ran pytest successfully with 100 % coverage" checklist |
| Docstring linting | Not enforced — `.flake8` ignores `D100`-`D105`, and `pydocstyle` is never invoked | `.flake8`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |

Documentation drift is significant enough to be a quality issue in its own right, and it runs in one direction — toward the superseded Node.js stack:

| Drifted Statement | Location | Repository Reality |
|---|---|---|
| Jest v29.7.0 configuration sample and `test/unit`, `test/integration`, `test/fixtures`, `test/helpers` tree | `CONTRIBUTING.md` L511-L570 | No `jest.config.js`; tests live flat in `src/backend/tests/` |
| "All tests pass: `npm test`", `npm run test:coverage`, `npm run test:ci` | `CONTRIBUTING.md` L962-L963; `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` L229-L261 | No `package.json`; the command is `pytest` |
| "Supertest v7.1.1 used for HTTP endpoint testing" | `CONTRIBUTING.md` L967 | Flask test client and `requests` are used |
| `tests/conftest.py` and `tests/test_endpoints.py` described | `src/backend/README.md` L591-L610 | Neither file exists |
| Example asserting `response.data == b'Hello world'` with `text/plain` | `README.md` L448-L456 | `/hello` returns JSON; the real tests assert `application/json` |
| Performance gates of `<100 ms`, `<50 MB`, `<5 s` startup | `CONTRIBUTING.md` L973-L975; `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` | Suite asserts `<50 ms` and `<75 MB` |
| `pytest-watch` watch-mode command | `README.md` L403 | Not declared in any manifest |

The one contributor-facing document that is fully migrated is `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md`, which asks for Python, pip, Flask, pytest and Gunicorn versions and gives pytest-based reproduction commands.


### 6.6.7 Security Testing Requirements

#### 6.6.7.1 Automated Security Scanning

Security testing is the second-most-developed layer after functional testing: five scanners run across the two pipelines, and four of them can block. Section 6.4 owns the security architecture; the table below documents the *testing* obligations each scanner imposes.

| Scanner | Invocation and Configuration | Gating Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Bandit (SAST) | `bandit -r src/` in JSON and SARIF modes, then `bandit -r src/ --severity-level medium`; `[tool.bandit]` excludes `tests`, `venv`, `.venv`, `build`, `dist`, `.pytest_cache`, `htmlcov` and skips `B101`, `B601`, `B602` | Report runs are `|| true`; the medium-severity run blocks the `security` job. `quality-gate` additionally fails on any HIGH finding |
| Safety (dependency CVEs) | `safety check --json --output safety-report.json || true`, then `safety check --short-report` | Enforcement run blocks; `quality-gate` fails on any recorded vulnerability |
| pip-audit (dependency CVEs) | JSON and SARIF reports `|| true`, then bare `pip-audit` | Enforcement run blocks the job |
| OSSF Scorecard (supply chain) | `ossf/scorecard-action@v2` with `results_format: sarif`, `publish_results: true` | Advisory; results published to code scanning |
| Trivy (container image) | `aquasecurity/trivy-action@master` against the image **digest**, `severity: CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW`, `exit-code: '0'` | Deliberately non-failing; a `jq`-based step evaluates the gate |
| flake8-security | `S` codes selected and enabled in `.flake8`, executed through the blocking `flake8` step | Blocks the matrix leg, but `S101`/`S105`/`S106`/`S311` are ignored for test files |

The CD security gate is threshold-based rather than binary (`.github/workflows/cd.yml` L395-L405): it fails when `CRITICAL > 0` **or** any Safety vulnerability is present, warns when `HIGH > 5` or Bandit issues exceed 3, and otherwise passes; when the SARIF file is absent it records `security_gate=unknown` and does not fail. All findings are uploaded to GitHub code scanning via `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2` with `if: always()`, and the raw reports are retained as the 90-day `security-reports` artifact.

#### 6.6.7.2 In-Suite Security Assertions

The pytest suite asserts the application's security posture directly, so a regression in hardening fails the test job rather than only appearing in a scanner report.

| Security Property | Asserted Expectation | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Response hardening headers | `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'`, `X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies: none` — presence **and** exact value | `test_app.py` L348-L367 |
| Server fingerprint suppression | Neither `Server` nor `X-Powered-By` may appear in any response | `test_app.py` L369-L379, reinforced at L143-L165 |
| CORS behaviour | Simple `GET` succeeds; `OPTIONS` preflight with `Access-Control-Request-Method`/`-Headers` returns 200 | `test_app.py` L381-L399 |
| CSRF posture under test | `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED` must be `False` in the testing configuration | `test_app.py` L65-L81; `env` blocks in all three pytest configs |
| Debug suppression | Production factory must yield `DEBUG is False` and `TESTING is False` | `test_app.py` L65-L81 |
| Error-envelope discipline | 404/405/500 responses return structured JSON with `status` and `error` fields rather than stack traces | `test_app.py` L237-L340 |
| Statelessness | No session cookie is set across repeated requests | `test_app.py` L507-L521 |

The `security` marker is declared in root `pytest.ini`, `src/backend/pytest.ini` and `pyproject.toml`, and `src/backend/pytest.ini` even declares `security_markers = security`, yet **no test applies it** — `TestFlaskSecurityConfiguration` is reached only through the module-level `unit`/`flask` markers. `pytest -m security` therefore selects nothing, and `src/backend/README.md`'s "Security Tests" category is realised as a class name rather than as a selectable marker.

#### 6.6.7.3 Test-Code Security Exemptions

Security tooling is deliberately relaxed for test code, and the exemptions are declared in three places:

| Exemption | Declaration | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Bandit skips assertion checks in tests | `[tool.bandit] skips = ["B101", …]` and `[tool.bandit.assert_used] exclude = ["**/test_*.py", "tests/**"]` | `assert` statements in tests are not flagged |
| Bandit excludes the tests directory | `[tool.bandit] exclude_dirs` includes `tests` | Test code is not scanned at all |
| flake8 relaxes security codes for tests | `.flake8` per-file-ignores add `S101`, `S311` (and `S105`, `S106` in the `pyproject.toml` mirror) | Hard-coded test secrets and asserts do not fail lint |

These exemptions are consistent with the fixtures, which set `SECRET_KEY='test-secret-key'` (`test_app.py` L630) while root `pytest.ini` supplies `SECRET_KEY = testing-secret-key-not-for-production` — values that would otherwise trip hard-coded-secret checks.

#### 6.6.7.4 Security Testing Gaps

The following security-testing categories are absent, verified by searching the workflows and manifests:

| Category | Status | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| DAST / active endpoint probing | Absent | No OWASP ZAP, Nikto or equivalent in any workflow or manifest |
| Secret scanning | Absent | No `gitleaks`, `trufflehog` or secret-scanning workflow step |
| CodeQL semantic analysis | Absent | Only `codeql-action/upload-sarif` is used; `codeql-action/analyze` never runs |
| Dependency review on pull requests | Absent | No `dependency-review-action`; no `dependabot.yml` or `renovate.json` |
| Authentication / authorization tests | Not applicable | Both routes are anonymous; no auth layer exists to test |
| Input-validation / fuzz testing | Absent | Neither route accepts a body or query parameter that the suite exercises; no fuzzing tool declared |
| Container runtime hardening tests | Partially covered | `docker-compose.yml` L563-L570 documents manual verification commands (`whoami`, capability inspection, read-only filesystem probe, network-isolation ping); no automated test executes them |
| Workflow permission hardening | Absent | `ci.yml` declares no `permissions` block |

The practical consequence is that security testing in this repository is strong on *static and dependency* analysis and weak on *dynamic* analysis: the running application's hardening is verified only through the response-header assertions in 6.6.7.2 and the deployed-environment 404 check in the CD smoke suites.


### 6.6.8 Test Environment Architecture and Resource Requirements

#### 6.6.8.1 Test Environment Matrix

Four environments can execute or verify tests. Only the first three run pytest; the fourth is verified by shell probes.

| Environment | Provisioning | Test Capability |
|---|---|---|
| Local virtual environment | `python3 -m venv .venv` then `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt` (or `pip install -e .[dev]`) | Full suite, including Gunicorn subprocess tests; requires `gunicorn` on `PATH` |
| Container `development` stage | `docker build --target development -t flask-tutorial:test .`; run `docker-compose run --rm flask-tutorial-dev python -m pytest` | Full suite inside `python:3.12-alpine` with `PYTHONPATH=/usr/src/app`; build fails unless pytest, pytest-flask and coverage import |
| CI runners | `ubuntu-latest` × `actions/setup-python@v4` for 3.12, 3.10 and 3.11 | Full suite per leg plus coverage/JUnit/HTML reporting and the coverage gate |
| Deployed Azure Web Apps | `azure/webapps-deploy@v2` with the digest-pinned production image | No pytest; `curl`-based health gates, smoke suites and the stability watch |

Environment configuration is applied consistently across the first three: `FLASK_ENV=testing`, `TESTING=1`, `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED=False`, `LOG_LEVEL=ERROR` from the pytest `env` blocks, with CI adding `CI=true`, `COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=100`, `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` and `FORCE_COLOR=1`. The deployed environments run the opposite profile — `FLASK_ENV=production`, `FLASK_DEBUG=false`, staging with `GUNICORN_WORKERS: 2` and production with `GUNICORN_WORKERS: 4` — which is precisely why their smoke thresholds are expressed in seconds rather than milliseconds.

**Diagram 6.6.8-A — Test environment architecture: the four environments, what each provisions, and which verification each performs.**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph LocalEnv["Local developer environment"]
        Venv[".venv from requirements-dev.txt<br/>pytest 8.4+, pytest-flask, pytest-cov,<br/>pytest-benchmark, psutil, requests"]
        LocalRun["pytest / pytest -v / pytest -k<br/>pytest --no-cov for fast iteration"]
        LocalGun["Gunicorn subprocess on an<br/>ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port"]
    end

    subgraph ContainerEnv["Container test environment - infrastructure/docker"]
        DevStage["Dockerfile target development<br/>python:3.12-alpine, non-root user<br/>self-verifies pytest, pytest-flask, coverage"]
        Compose["flask-tutorial-dev service<br/>source bind mount, venv and pip cache volumes<br/>no CPU or memory ceiling declared"]
        ProdSvc["flask-tutorial-prod service<br/>128M memory limit, 0.5 CPU<br/>75M reservation, 0.25 CPU"]
    end

    subgraph CIEnv["CI environment - ci.yml"]
        Runner["ubuntu-latest runners<br/>test job 15 min, security 10 min,<br/>quality-gate 10 min"]
        MatrixLegs["Three concurrent legs<br/>Python 3.12, 3.11, 3.10<br/>pip cache keyed on both manifests"]
        Reports["coverage.xml, coverage.json, htmlcov,<br/>junit.xml, pytest_report.html"]
    end

    subgraph DeployedEnv["Deployed environments - cd.yml"]
        Staging["Azure Web App staging<br/>2 Gunicorn workers, 45s warm-up<br/>12-attempt health gate"]
        Production["Azure Web App production<br/>4 Gunicorn workers, 75s warm-up<br/>18-attempt health gate"]
        Probes["curl smoke suites and<br/>12-check stability watch"]
    end

    Venv --> LocalRun
    LocalRun --> LocalGun
    DevStage --> Compose
    Compose -->|"docker-compose run --rm ... python -m pytest"| DevStage
    Runner --> MatrixLegs
    MatrixLegs --> Reports
    Reports -->|"artifacts and Codecov"| Gate["quality-gate validation<br/>line and branch rate at 100 percent"]
    Gate -->|"CI success on main"| Staging
    Staging --> Probes
    Probes --> Production
    ProdSvc -.->|"local production parity,<br/>not exercised by pytest"| Probes
```

#### 6.6.8.2 Resource Requirements for Test Execution

Resource requirements are stated only where the repository declares or implies them; no capacity figure below is inferred from convention.

| Resource Dimension | Declared or Implied Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Interpreter | CPython 3.12 for the primary leg; 3.11 and 3.10 also exercised | `ci.yml` matrix; `pyproject.toml` `requires-python = ">=3.12"` |
| Process memory ceiling asserted by tests | 75 MB RSS, with growth budgets of 5/10/20 MB | `test_app.py` L426-L427, L690; `test_wsgi.py` L188-L189, L843 |
| Declared memory monitor limits | `limit_mb = 75`, `growth_limit_mb = 5`; `memory_threshold_mb = 75` | `pyproject.toml` `[tool.memory-monitor]`; `src/backend/pytest.ini` |
| Container envelope for production-parity runs | 128 M limit / 75 M reservation; 0.5 CPU limit / 0.25 CPU reservation | `docker-compose.yml` L279-L286 |
| CPU parallelism | 3 concurrent CI legs; in-test `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10)`; Gunicorn 1-2 workers in tests | `ci.yml`; `test_app.py` L442; `test_wsgi.py` |
| Network | Loopback only for pytest (ephemeral ports 1024-65535); public HTTPS for CD probes | `dynamic_port` fixture; `cd.yml` |
| Per-test wall-clock limit | `timeout = 300` s, `timeout_method = thread` | All three pytest configs |
| Job wall-clock limits | test 15 min, security 10 min, quality-gate 10 min; CD build 20 / scan 15 / staging 12 / production 18 / notify 5 min | `ci.yml`, `cd.yml` |
| E2E internal budgets | Startup polls 10-15 s; load phase 10 s; shutdown 10 s; total lifecycle < 60 s | `test_wsgi.py` |
| Disk / artifact footprint | `htmlcov/`, `coverage.xml`, `coverage.json`, `junit.xml`, `pytest_report.html`, `tests.log`, `.pytest_cache/` — all git-ignored | `.gitignore` L140-L165; `src/backend/.gitignore` L27-L35 |
| Retention | 30 days for coverage/test artifacts, 90 days for security artifacts | `ci.yml` |

Two practical constraints follow. First, the Gunicorn-based tests require `gunicorn` to be installed and invocable as `python -m gunicorn`, and they must run from a working directory where `src.backend.wsgi:application` is importable — a requirement the CI configuration does not satisfy (6.6.9). Second, the absolute 75 MB RSS assertions measure the whole interpreter, including pytest, its plugins and coverage instrumentation, so headroom shrinks as the plugin set grows; the container production reservation is exactly 75 M, leaving no margin between the asserted ceiling and the reserved allocation.

#### 6.6.8.3 Test Data Flow

Test "data" in this system is configuration, generated resources and measurements rather than persisted records. The flow below traces every input from its source to the artifact that finally records it.

**Diagram 6.6.8-B — Test data flow: configuration and generated inputs entering the suite, and measurements leaving it as reports and gate decisions.**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Inputs["Test inputs - no persisted datasets exist"]
        IniEnv["pytest env blocks<br/>FLASK_ENV, TESTING,<br/>WTF_CSRF_ENABLED, LOG_LEVEL, SECRET_KEY"]
        DotEnv["load_dotenv('.env.testing')<br/>file absent - silent no-op"]
        Literals["Parametrize tables and literal expectations<br/>/hello, /health, 200, 404, 405,<br/>'Hello world', header values"]
        Generated["Generated at runtime<br/>ephemeral port via socket bind 0,<br/>psutil RSS baseline, perf_counter marks"]
    end

    subgraph Fixtures["Fixture layer - defined per module, no conftest.py"]
        SessionFix["configure_wsgi_test_environment<br/>session autouse: snapshot,<br/>apply profile, restore"]
        FuncFix["app / client / runner<br/>setup_test_environment autouse<br/>memory_monitor, dynamic_port,<br/>performance_baseline"]
    end

    subgraph Subjects["Systems under test"]
        Factory["create_testing_app / create_app('testing')<br/>DEBUG False, TESTING True, CSRF off"]
        TestClient["Flask test client<br/>in-process request context"]
        RealServer["Gunicorn subprocess<br/>src.backend.wsgi:application"]
    end

    subgraph Assertions["Assertion layer"]
        Contract["Contract checks<br/>status, JSON keys, header values"]
        Threshold["Threshold checks<br/>50ms / 100ms latency, 75MB RSS,<br/>growth budgets, success rate"]
    end

    subgraph Outputs["Recorded outputs"]
        Cov["coverage.xml / .json / htmlcov<br/>line and branch rates"]
        JUnit["junit.xml with all logging<br/>and passing tests recorded"]
        Html["pytest_report.html<br/>self-contained"]
        Logs["tests.log or logs/pytest.log<br/>DEBUG level, never uploaded"]
        Bench["benchmark statistics<br/>json_output declared,<br/>never archived"]
    end

    Decision{{"quality-gate decision<br/>coverage 100 percent and<br/>no HIGH security finding?"}}
    Promote["Promotion to CD<br/>build, scan, staging, production"]
    Block["Workflow failure<br/>artifacts retained for triage"]

    IniEnv --> FuncFix
    DotEnv --> SessionFix
    Literals --> Contract
    Generated --> FuncFix
    SessionFix --> FuncFix
    FuncFix --> Factory
    Factory --> TestClient
    FuncFix --> RealServer
    TestClient --> Contract
    RealServer --> Contract
    TestClient --> Threshold
    RealServer --> Threshold
    Contract --> JUnit
    Threshold --> Bench
    Contract --> Cov
    Threshold --> Logs
    Cov --> Decision
    JUnit --> Html
    Decision -->|"yes"| Promote
    Decision -->|"no"| Block
```

Three properties of this flow are worth stating explicitly. No test writes to a database, file store or external service, so there is nothing to clean up beyond environment variables and child processes. Every expected value is a literal in the test source, so the suite has no golden files, snapshots or recorded HTTP cassettes to maintain — and no snapshot-update workflow. And the only measurement that survives the run in a comparable form is coverage, because `benchmark_results.json` and the DEBUG test log are never uploaded as artifacts.


### 6.6.9 Test Apparatus Defect and Divergence Register

Every item below is a verified property of the committed repository, established either by reading the file or by executing the configuration. They are recorded here because they determine the difference between the strategy the repository *describes* and the verification it currently *performs*.

#### 6.6.9.1 Blocking Defects

| Defect | Evidence | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Root `pytest.ini` does not parse | Running pytest from the repository root reports `ERROR: pytest.ini:200: unexpected line: ']'`; `collect_ignore` is written as a Python list literal at L187-L200 (it is a `conftest.py` variable, not an ini option) | The session aborts before collection; no test can run under the primary configuration |
| `src/backend/pytest.ini` does not parse | Running pytest from `src/backend` reports `ERROR: src/backend/pytest.ini:105: unexpected line: ']'` (same `collect_ignore` pattern at L96-L105) | The CI invocation path is equally blocked |
| `test_wsgi.py` calls `sys.exit(1)` on import failure | L52-L59 and L64-L71 print diagnostics then `sys.exit(1)`; with the ini repaired, collection fails with `INTERNALERROR … SystemExit: 1` | An unmet dependency aborts the entire session instead of skipping one module — unlike `test_app.py`, which uses `pytest.skip(..., allow_module_level=True)` |
| Import paths do not match the module layout | `test_app.py` imports `src.app`; `test_wsgi.py` imports `src.backend.app`/`src.backend.wsgi`; the modules are at `src/backend/app.py` and `src/backend/wsgi.py`, and the repository contains **zero** `__init__.py` files | Verified by `importlib`: `src.backend.*` resolves only with the repository root on `sys.path`; `src.app` never resolves. `test_app.py` therefore always degrades to a module-level skip |
| CI runs pytest from the wrong directory for those imports | `working-directory: src/backend` with `--cov=src` | From `src/backend`, `src.*` is not importable and the coverage target `src` does not exist; the coverage gate cannot be satisfied by a passing run |
| CI installs a manifest that is not present | `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt` executed with `working-directory: src/backend`, where only `requirements.txt` exists | The dev/test toolchain installation step fails or silently installs the wrong set |

#### 6.6.9.2 Configuration Divergences

| Divergence | Evidence | Effect on Testing |
|---|---|---|
| Three competing pytest configurations | Root `pytest.ini`, `src/backend/pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` | pytest loads exactly one; the `pyproject.toml` profile is always shadowed by whichever `pytest.ini` is found first |
| `--cov-config=.coveragerc` references a missing file | Root `pytest.ini`; no `.coveragerc` exists at either candidate path | The `[tool.coverage.*]` settings in `pyproject.toml` are not loaded from the referenced path |
| Missing ini-option providers under `--strict-config` | `timeout`/`timeout_method` need `pytest-timeout`, declared in **no** manifest; `env` needs `pytest-env`, declared only in root `requirements-dev.txt` | Unknown ini options are escalated to errors, so a partially installed environment fails at startup |
| Marker sets differ and `--strict-markers` is active everywhere | `benchmark` declared only in root `pytest.ini`; `wsgi` declared only in `src/backend/pytest.ini`; neither is in the `pyproject.toml` marker list | Whichever configuration loads, at least one applied marker is undeclared and errors |
| Large blocks of non-standard ini keys | `src/backend/pytest.ini` declares `custom_outcomes`, `security_markers`, `flask_app`, `memory_profiling`, `max_workers`, `distributed_testing`, `integration_timeout`, `container_testing`, `e2e_timeout`, `quality_gate_*`, `exclude_lines`, `archive_*`, `asyncio_mode = auto` (with `pytest-asyncio` declared nowhere), and more | None affect execution; they read as specification prose inside a machine-consumed file, and they conflict with `--strict-config` |
| Interpreter matrix contradicts the declared floor | `requires-python = ">=3.12"` versus matrix legs 3.11 and 3.10 | Two of three legs test an unsupported interpreter |
| `minversion` disagreement | `8.0` in root `pytest.ini`, `7.0` in `src/backend/pytest.ini` | Different minimum runner versions depending on invocation directory |
| CI writes into a non-existent directory | `quality-gate` heredocs `scripts/validate_coverage.py` under `src/backend`, then `mkdir -p scripts` after the write | Order-dependent; `src/backend/scripts/` is not in the repository |

#### 6.6.9.3 Test-Code Defects

| Defect | Location | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Patch target is not a module attribute | `patch('src.app.hello_route_handler', …)` — the function is nested inside `register_route_handlers` (`src/backend/app.py` L368) | The intended 500-path simulation cannot bind; the test falls back to invoking `app.error_handler_spec` directly, as its own comment concedes |
| Non-existent pytest API used in a fixture | `pytest.warn(...)` in the autouse slow-test guard (`test_app.py` L670); `pytest` exposes no `warn` attribute (verified) | The guard raises `AttributeError` whenever a test exceeds 1 000 ms, converting a soft warning into a hard error |
| Module-level `pytest_plugins` | `test_wsgi.py` L1397 | Ignored by modern pytest outside the rootdir `conftest.py`; plugin availability depends on installation, not this declaration |
| Duplicated, divergent fixtures | `memory_monitor` defined in both modules with different tolerances (10 MB vs 10 MB/75 MB combinations) | Divergence is invisible without a shared `conftest.py` |
| Referenced environment file absent | `load_dotenv('.env.testing')` (`test_wsgi.py` L101) | Silent no-op; effective values come from the fixture's explicit `os.environ.update` |
| Benchmark result handling | `benchmark.pedantic(...)` return value is asserted as if it were a response object (`test_app.py` L469-L473) | Depends on `pedantic` returning the wrapped call's value; brittle against plugin behaviour changes |

#### 6.6.9.4 Consequences for the Documented Strategy

Read together, the register produces one conclusion that must not be lost in the detail: **the 100 % coverage figure asserted throughout the repository is a configured target, not an observed result.** The suite as committed cannot complete a run — the configuration fails to parse, and once repaired the WSGI module aborts the session or the application imports resolve to nothing — so no coverage measurement can currently reach the gate. The illustrative coverage tables in `README.md` L437-L444 and `src/backend/README.md` L457-L465, and the `TOTAL … 100%` sample in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md`, are hand-written examples rather than captured output.

The repository's own status document is consistent with this reading: `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` records 15 of 100 estimated engineering hours outstanding, with the highest-priority item described as examining the generated Python code for syntax errors, fixing pip dependency issues and ensuring "all Python imports are correct", and a separate item allocating time to run pytest-benchmark to verify the sub-50 ms and sub-75 MB targets. The smallest change set implied by the evidence above is: remove the two `collect_ignore` blocks, replace `sys.exit(1)` with `pytest.skip(..., allow_module_level=True)`, converge the test imports and the `--cov` target on one layout, and either create `.coveragerc` or drop the `--cov-config` flag. Nothing in this sub-section is a commitment; it records what the evidence shows and what the existing seams would require.
