#### 9.2.3.1 Four-Rung Enforcement Ladder

The enforcement guidelines (L135-L166) follow the Contributor Covenant's four-tier structure, with an **Educational Component** added to every rung — the project's principal adaptation of the upstream text:

| Rung | Consequence | Educational Component |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Correction (L138) | Private written warning; a public apology may be requested | Guidance on appropriate communication plus improvement resources |
| 2. Warning (L144) | Warning with consequences; a no-interaction period covering community spaces and external channels | Required communication workshop or mentoring session |
| 3. Temporary Ban (L152) | Time-boxed ban on all public and private interaction | Completion of community-standards education before reinstatement is considered |
| 4. Permanent Ban (L160) | Permanent ban from public interaction | No reinstatement; educational resources still provided |

#### 9.2.3.2 Attribution and Contact Record

The attribution block (L332-L342) records five distinct claims: adaptation from Contributor Covenant 2.1; an enumeration of the added educational sections; community input from "the Node.js educational community"; a version statement — "Version 1.0 – Initial release aligned with Node.js v22.16.0 LTS and Express.js v5.1.0 tutorial project launch"; and MIT-licence compatibility. The contact block (L346-L354) gives the enforcement address `project-maintainers@example.com`, a community type of "Educational Open Source", and the project name "Node.js Hello World Tutorial".

Both contact addresses in the governance layer are placeholders on example domains — `project-maintainers@example.com` here and the security address recorded in `6.5.3.2` — so neither the conduct-reporting nor the vulnerability-reporting channel is operable as committed.

### 9.2.4 Issue and Pull Request Intake Templates

`.github/` contains exactly three intake artefacts and nothing else besides `workflows/`: two issue templates and one pull-request template. There is no `config.yml` in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, so blank issues are not disabled and no external contact links are offered; both templates are legacy Markdown templates with YAML front matter rather than GitHub issue *forms*, which means every field is free text and none is validated.

| Template | Front Matter | Labels Applied |
|---|---|---|
| `bug_report.md` (492 lines) | name "Bug Report"; about references the **Python Flask** tutorial application; title prefix `[BUG]` | `bug`, `needs-triage` |
| `feature_request.md` (389 lines) | name "Feature Request"; about references the **Node.js** tutorial application; title prefix `[FEATURE]` | `enhancement`, `needs-evaluation` |
| `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (508 lines) | none (pull-request templates take no front matter) | — |

The `about` fields expose a **partially completed migration**: the bug-report template was rewritten for Flask while the feature-request template was not. Neither declares assignees.

#### 9.2.4.1 Section Inventories

| Template | Sections | Structural Volume |
|---|---|---|
| `bug_report.md` | Bug Summary L13; Environment Information L26; Steps to Reproduce L49; Expected Behavior L92; Actual Behavior L102; Error Logs and Output L116; Configuration Details L154; Testing Information L179; Issue Isolation L217; Additional Context L245; Educational Impact L264; Pre-submission Checklist L278; Development Setup Guidelines L297; Bug Categories Reference L364; Flask-Specific Troubleshooting L381 | 15 H2, 13 H3, 43 checkboxes, 28 code fences |
| `feature_request.md` | Feature Summary L11; Problem Statement L21; Proposed Solution L44; Educational Alignment L68; Implementation Details L101; Alternatives Considered L151; Use Cases and Examples L171; Impact Assessment L207; Acceptance Criteria L231; Feature Category L255; Additional Context L289; Priority and Timeline L308; Community Engagement L332; Compatibility Declaration L349 | 14 H2, 31 H3, 2 H4, 74 checkboxes, 4 code fences |
| `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` | Title banner L2; Summary of Changes L8; Type of Change L28; Educational Alignment L58; Technical Implementation L122; Testing L209; Documentation L284; Quality Checklist L352; Additional Information L476; Pre-submission Checklist L492 | 10 H2, 28 H3, 98 checkboxes, 2 code fences |

The three templates together present **215 manual checkboxes** — 98 in the pull-request template alone. That is an order of magnitude more manual verification than the repository has automated gates, and it is the mechanism through which the stale Node-era acceptance criteria recorded in `6.5.2.4` continue to be presented to reviewers. The pull-request template's own banner (L2) still reads `## Node.js Hello World Tutorial Application`.

Notably, `bug_report.md` is the most operationally useful of the three: it is the only artefact in the repository that publishes a verbatim example of the real log line format (L116-L152), it enumerates a ten-category triage taxonomy (L364-L380), and its Flask-Specific Troubleshooting section (L381-L492) contains the diagnostic invocations catalogued in `9.1.6.3`.

#### 9.2.5.2 The Retained Pre-Migration Specification

`Technical Specifications_b3815ee7-12a2-46a4-a950-4b8e72ef8030.md` (4,876 lines, 185.4 KiB) is the **Node.js/Express specification that preceded this document**. It is retained unmodified and is cited throughout this specification as evidence of documented intent — for example the monitoring determination reproduced in `6.5` and the Node-era metric and SLO tables compared there.

Its top-level structure comprises eight numbered sections — 1. INTRODUCTION (L3), 2. PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS (L189), 3. TECHNOLOGY STACK (L527), 4. PROCESS FLOWCHART (L768), 5. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE (L1398), 6. SYSTEM COMPONENTS DESIGN (L1834), 7. USER INTERFACE DESIGN (L4057), 8. INFRASTRUCTURE (L4222) — plus 54 second-level headings. Three structural properties are relevant when reading citations to it:

- **Section 6 contains two overlapping 6.1-6.5 series.** The first (L1836-L2176) runs COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE, DETAILED COMPONENT SPECIFICATIONS, DATA FLOW ARCHITECTURE, INTEGRATION INTERFACES, SECURITY ARCHITECTURE; the second (L2247-L3539) runs CORE SERVICES ARCHITECTURE, DATABASE DESIGN, INTEGRATION ARCHITECTURE, SECURITY ARCHITECTURE, MONITORING AND OBSERVABILITY, TESTING STRATEGY. A bare citation of "Section 6.4" in that document is therefore ambiguous.
- **Its section 4 and section 8 outlines differ from the current document**: section 4 adds 4.4 ERROR HANDLING (L1128), 4.5 INTEGRATION SEQUENCE DIAGRAMS (L1257), and 4.6 PERFORMANCE AND TIMING CONSTRAINTS (L1347); section 8 runs to 8.8 and includes 8.6 COST CONSIDERATIONS (L4525) and 8.7 MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES (L4550).
- **One heading is an artefact**: `# Basic GET request` at L4158 is a shell comment inside a fenced block that renders as a first-level heading.

### 9.2.6 Estimated Effort Distribution and Completion Accounting

`blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` is 37 lines long and is the repository's only delivery-status record. `2.4.6` owns the deferred-work allocation — the eight outstanding tasks with their priorities, hour estimates, and affected features — and is not repeated here. What that section does not publish is the **completed-effort distribution**, which is the more informative half of the document for anyone reasoning about where this repository's engineering weight sits.

| Workstream (as labelled in the document) | Hours | Delivered Artefacts |
|---|---|---|
| Core application development (app.js, server.js) | 25 | `src/backend/app.py` (750 lines), `src/backend/wsgi.py` (530) |
| Test suite implementation (server.test.js, app.test.js) | 20 | `src/backend/tests/test_wsgi.py` (1,405), `tests/test_app.py` (712) |
| Docker containerization (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml) | 15 | `infrastructure/docker/` (1,614 lines across three files) |
| CI/CD pipelines (ci.yml, cd.yml) | 15 | `.github/workflows/` (1,422 lines) |
| Documentation (README.md, package.json) | 10 | `README.md` (1,002), `src/backend/README.md` (1,004), `requirements.txt` (27) |
| **Completed subtotal** | **85** | 85 % of a 100-hour estimate |

The arithmetic is internally consistent: 25 + 20 + 15 + 15 + 10 = 85, matching the stated 85 %, and the eight outstanding tasks in `2.4.6` sum to exactly 15. The document renders the split as a mermaid pie chart (L3-L7) and describes the residual 15 hours under five themes: final production-readiness tasks, dependency validation and updates, environment configuration, security hardening, and performance optimisation.

Two observations follow from the labelling. First, **every workstream is named after its Node.js predecessor file** — `app.js`, `server.js`, `server.test.js`, `app.test.js`, `package.json` — even though each was delivered as a Python artefact. The status record therefore shares the incomplete-migration characteristic of the governance documents rather than reflecting the delivered file set. Second, the estimate allocates **40 of 85 hours (47 %) to container and pipeline work** against 25 hours of application development, which is proportionate to what the repository actually contains: 3,036 lines of container and workflow assets versus 1,280 lines of runtime code (`9.1.1.3`).


## 9.3 Glossary

The terms below are those used in this specification whose meaning is specific to this system, to the Python/Flask stack it targets, or to the migration it documents. Each definition is scoped to how the term is actually used in this repository rather than to its most general industry sense, and the third column names the artefact or specification section that establishes it. This glossary supersedes `A.2 GLOSSARY` in the retained pre-migration specification (`9.2.5.3`), whose terms describe the Node.js/Express predecessor.

Acronyms are expanded separately in `9.4`.

### 9.3.1 Architecture and Runtime Terms

| Term | Definition as Used in This System | Established By |
|---|---|---|
| Application factory pattern | A module-level function (`create_app`) that constructs and returns a configured `Flask` instance on demand, rather than instantiating a global application at import time. Enables a distinct configuration profile per invocation and per test. | `src/backend/app.py`; `5.2` |
| WSGI callable | The Python object a WSGI server invokes with the `(environ, start_response)` protocol defined by PEP 3333. In this system it is the Flask application returned by the factory. | `src/backend/wsgi.py`; `6.3` |
| Application object | The specific module-level name a server command must reference. This system exports it as `application` (`wsgi.py` L531, `__all__`), which is why the eleven `wsgi:app` command strings catalogued in `9.1.6.1` cannot start. | `src/backend/wsgi.py` |
| Request-lifecycle hook | A function registered with `before_request` or `after_request` that runs around every view invocation. This system uses one of each: the first stamps the request with a start time and correlation identifier, the second computes elapsed time and attaches response headers. | `src/backend/app.py`; `4.1` |
| Error handler | A function registered with `@app.errorhandler` for a specific HTTP status class. Four exist (404, 405, 500, plus a generic handler), and each returns the same JSON envelope shape. | `src/backend/app.py`; `5.2` |
| Error envelope | The uniform JSON body returned by every error handler, echoing the caller's own path and method and omitting internal detail. The primary information-disclosure control in the application. | `src/backend/app.py`; `2.4.4` |
| Configuration profile | One of three named configuration branches — `development`, `production`, `testing` — selected by `FLASK_ENV`. The base configuration is applied first and the profile overlays it; an unrecognised name yields base configuration only. | `src/backend/app.py`; `2.4.1` |
| Cold start | Elapsed time from process launch to the first successful response, measured against a 100 ms threshold in the WSGI test suite. Distinguished from *warm response* because the two are measured by different instruments. | `Input Prompt.md` L35; `tests/test_wsgi.py` |
| Warm response | Per-request latency once the process is initialised, asserted below 50 ms through the Flask test client and a loopback Gunicorn process. Not measured in any deployed environment. | `tests/test_app.py`; `6.5.2.2` |
| Graceful shutdown | Handling of SIGTERM/SIGINT so that in-flight work completes and shutdown is logged before the process exits, rather than terminating abruptly. In this system the handler performs logging only — no resource release is implemented. | `src/backend/wsgi.py`; `2.4.1` |
| Sync pre-fork worker model | The Gunicorn worker class used here (`--worker-class=sync`): each worker handles exactly one request at a time, so effective concurrency equals worker count. No async worker class or thread pool is configured. | `infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile`; `2.4.3` |
| Worker recycling | Gunicorn's bounded worker lifetime (`--max-requests=1000 --max-requests-jitter=100`): each worker is retired after roughly 1,000 requests, with jitter so that workers do not retire simultaneously. | `infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile` |
| Preload | The Gunicorn `--preload` flag, which imports the application in the arbiter before forking workers. Reduces per-worker memory and surfaces import errors at start-up rather than per worker. | `infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile` |
| Init process (PID 1) | The process that receives signals and reaps orphaned children inside a container. This system installs `dumb-init` as PID 1 so that SIGTERM reaches Gunicorn and the `wsgi.py` handlers. | `infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile`; `3.6.5` |

### 9.3.2 HTTP and API Terms

| Term | Definition as Used in This System | Established By |
|---|---|---|
| Preflight request | The `OPTIONS` request a browser issues before a cross-origin request, answered here by Flask-CORS from a fixed allow-list with a 24-hour `max_age`. | `src/backend/app.py`; `6.3` |
| Origin allow-list | The explicit, wildcard-free set of origins permitted for cross-origin access — here only `http://localhost:3000` and `http://localhost:8000`, so no deployed browser origin is permitted. | `src/backend/app.py`; `2.4.1` |
| Security response header | One of the six fixed headers attached to every response, plus the removal of `Server`. Their values are compile-time constants with no environment override. | `src/backend/app.py`; `6.4` |
| Correlation identifier | The per-request token `req_<epoch-milliseconds>` assigned in the `before_request` hook, returned as `X-Request-ID` and echoed in the 500 envelope. Not globally unique and not a trace identifier. | `src/backend/app.py` L316; `6.5.1.4` |
| Health endpoint | `GET /health`, which returns a JSON status document constructed from literals and configuration reads. It performs no dependency verification because the service has no dependency. | `src/backend/app.py`; `6.5.2.1` |
| Liveness probe | A periodic check that determines whether a container should be restarted. In this system all five container-level probes target `/hello`, not `/health`. | `infrastructure/docker/`; `6.5.2.1` |
| Readiness probe | A check that determines whether an instance should receive traffic. Only the test suite uses `/health` this way; no runtime consumer distinguishes ready from live. | `tests/test_wsgi.py`; `6.5.2.1` |
| Startup probe | A grace period during which probe failures are suppressed. Approximated here by `HEALTHCHECK --start-period` values and by fixed pre-probe sleeps in the deployment jobs. | `infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile`; `.github/workflows/cd.yml` |
| Smoke test | A single post-deployment assertion executed by the delivery pipeline against a live URL — body content, status code, media type, latency, or the 404 path. | `.github/workflows/cd.yml`; `8.5` |
| Health gate | A bounded retry loop in the deployment pipeline that must succeed before a release proceeds: twelve attempts for staging, eighteen for production. | `.github/workflows/cd.yml`; `6.5.1.5` |
| Media type | The `Content-Type` of a response. Every response body in this system is produced by `jsonify()`, so `application/json` is the only media type emitted. | `src/backend/app.py`; `6.3` |

### 9.3.3 Container and Delivery Terms

| Term | Definition as Used in This System | Established By |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-stage build | A single Dockerfile defining several named stages so that build-time tooling need not appear in the runtime image. This Dockerfile defines five stages, of which `production` derives from `application` rather than from a clean base. | `infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile`; `8.3` |
| Build stage / target | A named `FROM … AS <name>` block, selectable at build time with `--target`. The delivery pipeline builds `target: production`; Compose builds `development` and `production`. | `infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile` |
| Build context | The file set sent to the builder. Trimmed here by a 762-line `.dockerignore` that excludes version control, virtual environments, caches, all `.env` files, keys, and IDE configuration. | `infrastructure/docker/.dockerignore`; `8.3` |
| Layer cache | Reuse of unchanged image layers across builds. Achieved here by ordering dependency installation before source copying, and in the pipeline by GitHub Actions cache (`type=gha`). | `infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile`; `.github/workflows/cd.yml` |
| Digest-addressed image | An image referenced by its content digest rather than a mutable tag, so the deployed artefact is immutable and identifiable. Both deployment jobs reference the digest emitted by the build job. | `.github/workflows/cd.yml`; `8.5` |
| Multi-architecture image | A published image built for more than one CPU architecture — here `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` via Buildx. | `.github/workflows/cd.yml`; `8.3` |
| Provenance attestation | Signed build-origin metadata attached to the published image (`provenance: true`), recording how and from what the image was produced. Attached to the image only; nothing is committed to the repository. | `.github/workflows/cd.yml`; `3.3.7` |
| Software bill of materials | A machine-readable inventory of the components inside the image, generated at publish time (`sbom: true`) and attached as an attestation. | `.github/workflows/cd.yml`; `3.3.7` |
| Named volume | A Compose-managed persistent volume referenced by name. Five are declared, principally for pip caches and scratch space. | `infrastructure/docker/docker-compose.yml`; `8.3` |
| Bind mount | A host directory mapped into a container. Used for the delegated source mount that makes hot reload work in the development service. | `infrastructure/docker/docker-compose.yml` |
| tmpfs mount | An in-memory filesystem mounted into a container, used here to provide writable scratch space to a service whose root filesystem is read-only. | `infrastructure/docker/docker-compose.yml`; `6.4` |
| Capability drop | Removal of Linux kernel capabilities from a container (`cap_drop: ALL`), with only the minimum restored (`SETGID`, `SETUID`). | `infrastructure/docker/docker-compose.yml`; `6.4` |
| Read-only root filesystem | A container whose image layers are mounted read-only at run time (`read_only: true`), so nothing outside the declared tmpfs mounts can be written. | `infrastructure/docker/docker-compose.yml`; `6.4` |
| Educational compromise | A hardening or design choice deliberately weakened for teaching purposes and annotated as such in the source — for example the `apparmor:unconfined` setting on the production Compose service and the millisecond correlation identifier. | `infrastructure/docker/docker-compose.yml`; `src/backend/app.py` |

### 9.3.4 Continuous Integration and Quality Terms

| Term | Definition as Used in This System | Established By |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrency group | A GitHub Actions key that serialises or cancels overlapping runs. CI cancels in-progress runs of the same ref; CD queues them (`cancel-in-progress: false`). | `.github/workflows/`; `8.5` |
| Matrix strategy | A job configuration that fans out across parameter values. The CI `test` job runs three Python versions (3.12, 3.11, 3.10), two of which are below the declared `requires-python` floor. | `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `2.4.1` |
| `workflow_run` trigger | A trigger that starts one workflow when another completes. CD is chained to the completion of "CI Pipeline" on `main` with a `success` conclusion. | `.github/workflows/cd.yml`; `8.5` |
| Workflow artefact | A file bundle uploaded from a run and retained for a fixed period. Five bundles exist here, at 30 or 90 days — the complete list is in `9.1.4.1`. | `.github/workflows/`; `6.5.1.1` |
| Quality gate | A pipeline step that fails the build when a measured value violates a threshold. The enforced gates here are 100 % line and branch coverage, medium-or-higher Bandit findings, any Safety or pip-audit finding, and any Trivy `CRITICAL`. | `.github/workflows/`; `3.6.6` |
| Non-blocking step | A step whose failure is suppressed, typically with `|| true`, so a tool crash cannot fail the job. Used for all security *report generation*, with a separate blocking invocation providing the actual gate. | `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `3.3.7` |
| Marker | A pytest label applied with `@pytest.mark.<name>` and declared in the ini file. The root configuration declares 17 markers and the backend 10; only three are actually applied in source. | `pytest.ini`; `src/backend/pytest.ini` |
| Fixture | A pytest-managed setup/teardown function injected into tests by parameter name. Eleven exist, defined inline per module because no `conftest.py` exists. | `src/backend/tests/`; `2.4.1` |
| Parametrisation | Generation of multiple test cases from one function via `@pytest.mark.parametrize`. Applied in `test_app.py` only. | `src/backend/tests/test_app.py` |
| Line coverage / branch coverage | The proportion of executable lines, respectively of conditional outcomes, exercised by the test suite. Both are enforced at 100 % — the branch dimension via `--cov-branch`. | `pytest.ini`; `6.6` |
| Fail-under threshold | The coverage floor below which pytest exits non-zero (`--cov-fail-under=100`), independently re-checked in CI against `COVERAGE_THRESHOLD: 100`. | `pytest.ini`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |
| Coverage context | A coverage.py feature (`--cov-context=test`) that records which test exercised each line, enabling per-test attribution in the HTML report. | `pytest.ini` |
| Declarative-only key | A configuration key that is syntactically valid but read by no tool in this repository. Approximately seventy-five exist; they are catalogued in `9.1.5`. | `pyproject.toml`; `src/backend/pytest.ini` |

### 9.3.5 Project-Specific Terms

| Term | Definition as Used in This System | Established By |
|---|---|---|
| `flask-migration-tutorial` | The distribution name declared in `pyproject.toml` and the canonical identifier for this system throughout the specification. Version `1.0.0`, static. | `pyproject.toml`; `1.1.1` |
| Migration provenance comment | A source comment of the form "Replaces `<Node/Express construct>` with `<Python/Flask construct>`". Seventy-nine occur across the four Python modules; they are the mechanism by which the migration mapping is delivered. | `src/backend/`; `9.1.1.6` |
| Log marker | The pictographic prefix that opens every log and `print` message in the runtime modules. Forty distinct markers are in use; the catalogue is `9.1.3`. | `src/backend/app.py`; `src/backend/wsgi.py` |
| Guarded import | A `try`/`except ImportError` block that prints a `pip install` remediation line before terminating. Three exist, with two distinct termination semantics — see `9.1.3.1`. | `src/backend/app.py`; `src/backend/wsgi.py` |
| Referenced-but-absent artefact | A file path that repository configuration or documentation depends on but that does not exist. Seventeen are registered in `9.1.4.2`. | `9.1.4.2` |
| Executable boundary | The set of directories containing code that actually runs — here `src/backend/` alone. Everything else is configuration, tests, documentation, container assets, workflows, or governance templates. | repository structure; `1.3` |
| Retained pre-migration specification | The unmodified Node.js/Express technical specification preserved at `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications_b3815ee7-…​.md`, cited throughout this document as evidence of documented intent rather than of current behaviour. | `blitzy/documentation/`; `9.2.5.2` |
| Human input | An outstanding task recorded in `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` that requires manual action to complete the system. Eight remain, totalling fifteen estimated hours. | `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md`; `2.4.6` |
| Declared-versus-enforced | The distinction, used throughout this specification, between a threshold or setting that appears in configuration and one that a tool or pipeline actually evaluates. | `2.4`; `9.1.5` |
| Twelve-factor configuration | The convention of supplying all deployment-varying configuration through environment variables rather than committed files, implemented here with `python-dotenv` and an `.env.example` template. | `src/backend/.env.example`; `3.3.2` |


## 9.4 Acronyms

Every abbreviation used in this specification is expanded below, together with the concrete artefact or section in which it is used. The three-column shape follows the convention established by `A.3 ACRONYMS` in the retained pre-migration specification (`9.2.5.3`), which this sub-section supersedes for the Python/Flask stack — the legacy inventory's runtime-specific entries (CommonJS, ECMAScript Modules, Technical Committee, OpenJS, ReDoS) have no analogue here.

The final table isolates abbreviations that appear **only as vocabulary of this specification** and not anywhere in the repository, so that they are never mistaken for repository facts.

### 9.4.1 Standards, Protocols, and Data Formats

| Acronym | Expanded Form | Context in This System |
|---|---|---|
| API | Application Programming Interface | The two-route HTTP contract documented in `6.3`; also the `X-API-Version: 1.0` response header |
| CORS | Cross-Origin Resource Sharing | Implemented with the `Flask-CORS` extension and a wildcard-free origin allow-list (`src/backend/app.py`) |
| CSP | Content Security Policy | Emitted as `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'` on every response |
| CSRF | Cross-Site Request Forgery | `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED=False` is set in the `testing` profile and in both `pytest.ini` `env` blocks |
| HTML | HyperText Markup Language | Generated report formats only — `htmlcov/` and `pytest_report.html`; the application serves no HTML |
| HTTP | HyperText Transfer Protocol | The only protocol the application speaks; both routes are `GET` |
| HTTPS | HTTP Secure | `PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME: 'https'` expresses a preference; the deployment gates call public HTTPS URLs |
| INI | Initialisation file format | The format of `pytest.ini`, `src/backend/pytest.ini`, and `.flake8` |
| JSON | JavaScript Object Notation | The only response media type (`jsonify()`); also the format of `coverage.json` and every security report |
| MIME | Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions | Referenced through `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, which disables MIME-type sniffing |
| PEP | Python Enhancement Proposal | PEP 3333 (WSGI), PEP 518 (build system), PEP 621 (project metadata), PEP 8 (style) — all four are cited in the repository or its manifests |
| REST | Representational State Transfer | The architectural style the two `GET` endpoints follow; no resource mutation exists |
| SARIF | Static Analysis Results Interchange Format | The format in which Bandit, pip-audit, OSSF Scorecard, and Trivy findings are uploaded to code scanning |
| SBOM | Software Bill of Materials | Generated at image publish time by `docker/build-push-action@v5` with `sbom: true` |
| SSL / TLS | Secure Sockets Layer / Transport Layer Security | Named in `.env.example` (`DATABASE_SSL_MODE`, commented out) and in `3.6.9`, which records that TLS provisioning remains manual |
| TOML | Tom's Obvious Minimal Language | The format of `pyproject.toml`; `tomli>=2.0.1` is floor-pinned for parsing it |
| URL | Uniform Resource Locator | The six `[project.urls]` entries, the deployment environment URLs, and every documented `curl` target |
| WSGI | Web Server Gateway Interface | The PEP 3333 server-to-application contract that `src/backend/wsgi.py` implements and Gunicorn consumes |
| XML | Extensible Markup Language | The format of `coverage.xml` and `junit.xml`; `lxml` is installed in the `quality-gate` job to parse the former |
| XSS | Cross-Site Scripting | Named in the security rationale for the response-header set; no template rendering exists to be exploited |
| YAML | YAML Ain't Markup Language | The format of the two workflow files, `docker-compose.yml`, and the issue-template front matter |

### 9.4.2 Platform, Runtime, and Infrastructure

| Acronym | Expanded Form | Context in This System |
|---|---|---|
| AMD64 | Advanced Micro Devices 64-bit (x86-64) | One of the two published image platforms (`linux/amd64`) |
| ARM64 | Advanced RISC Machines 64-bit (AArch64) | The second published image platform (`linux/arm64`) |
| CPU | Central Processing Unit | Compose limits and reservations (0.5 / 0.25 CPU); no code samples CPU utilisation |
| GHCR | GitHub Container Registry | The publication target, set as `REGISTRY: ghcr.io` in the CD workflow |
| GID | Group Identifier | The non-root group `1000` created in the Dockerfile `base` stage |
| IPAM | IP Address Management | The Compose bridge network configuration for `flask-br0` with subnet `172.21.0.0/16` |
| LTS | Long Term Support | The support classification of the Node.js v22.16.0 predecessor runtime, retained in the governance badges |
| MB | Megabyte | The unit of the 75 MB resident-memory target and the 128 MB container limit |
| OCI | Open Container Initiative | The label namespace applied to the published image (`org.opencontainers.image.*`) |
| OS | Operating System | The `Operating System :: OS Independent` classifier and the OS field in the bug-report environment block |
| PID | Process Identifier | Logged with every memory sample; also the `dumb-init` PID 1 arrangement |
| PyPI | Python Package Index | The default and only package index used; no private index is configured |
| RAM | Random Access Memory | The host-sizing table in `README.md` (75 / 150 MB) |
| RSS | Resident Set Size | The physical-memory figure sampled by `psutil` in `log_memory_usage` and compared to 75 MB |
| UID | User Identifier | The non-root user `1000` under which every container process runs |
| VMS | Virtual Memory Size | The virtual-memory figure sampled alongside RSS, logged but never compared to a threshold |
| venv | Virtual Environment | The stdlib isolation mechanism documented for local development and created inside the image at `/usr/src/app/.venv` |

### 9.4.3 Delivery, Quality, and Security Tooling

| Acronym | Expanded Form | Context in This System |
|---|---|---|
| APM | Application Performance Monitoring | Named only as a recommended future tool in `src/backend/README.md`; no APM client exists in any manifest |
| CD | Continuous Deployment | `.github/workflows/cd.yml`, the five-job build-scan-stage-production-notify pipeline |
| CI | Continuous Integration | `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the three-job test-security-quality-gate pipeline; also the `CI: true` workflow variable |
| CLI | Command Line Interface | The Flask CLI (`python -m flask run`) documented for development, provided transitively by `click` |
| E2E | End to End | The `e2e` pytest marker and the `e2e_timeout`/`e2e_retries`/`e2e_parallel` keys in `src/backend/pytest.ini` |
| IDE | Integrated Development Environment | Referenced in the mypy rationale ("enhanced IDE support") and excluded from the build context by `.dockerignore` |
| OSSF | Open Source Security Foundation | The publisher of Scorecard, invoked as `ossf/scorecard-action@v2` in the CI security job |
| QA | Quality Assurance | The "QA/Bug Fixes" task carrying the largest outstanding estimate in `Project Guide.md` |
| SCM | Source Code Management | The version-derivation mechanism declared as `[tool.setuptools_scm]`; inoperative because the repository has no tags |
| SDK | Software Development Kit | Used in this document to describe the absent tracing and telemetry client libraries (`6.5.1.4`) |
| SHA | Secure Hash Algorithm | The commit hash embedded by the `type=sha` image-tag directive in the CD metadata step |
| SLA | Service Level Agreement | Appears only inside test assertion messages and marker descriptions; no customer commitment exists (`6.5.2.4`) |
| VCS | Version Control System | The `VCS_REF` build argument passed by Compose — and discarded, because the Dockerfile declares no `ARG` |

### 9.4.4 Governance, Legacy Stack, and Specification-Only Vocabulary

| Acronym | Expanded Form | Context in This System |
|---|---|---|
| JWT | JSON Web Token | Present only as commented-out `.env.example` keys (`JWT_SECRET_KEY`, `JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRES`); no authentication is implemented |
| MIT | Massachusetts Institute of Technology (licence) | The permissive licence declared in `pyproject.toml` and reproduced in `README.md`; no `LICENSE` file exists (`9.2.1`) |
| npm | Node Package Manager | Node-era commands retained in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the pull-request template; no `package.json` exists |
| PR | Pull Request | The review unit governed by `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and by the weighted rubric in `9.2.2.3` |

The following abbreviations are used in this specification to describe capabilities the system **does not** have, and appear nowhere in the repository. They are listed so that their absence is unambiguous.

| Acronym | Expanded Form | Why It Appears in This Document |
|---|---|---|
| IaC | Infrastructure as Code | `3.6.9` and `8.x` record that no IaC layer exists — `infrastructure/` contains only `docker/` |
| SLO | Service Level Objective | `6.5.2.4` records that no objective, error budget, or burn-rate policy is defined |
| RPO / RTO | Recovery Point Objective / Recovery Time Objective | Used in the availability and recovery discussion in `5.4.6`; neither is declared in the repository |
| SEV | Severity (incident level) | `6.5.3.2` records the absence of any severity model or SEV-level definitions |
| SKU | Stock Keeping Unit (cloud pricing tier) | `8.7.4` records that the repository declares no cost, budget, SKU, or region |
